building_canonical_addresses.name: building_canonical_addresses
building_canonical_addresses.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fba.STREET_NUMBER AS ADDRESS_LINE1,
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL IS NOT NULL AND fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NAME IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NAME <> '' AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_SUFFIX <> '' THEN ' ' ELSE '' END,
    COALESCE(fba.STREET_SUFFIX, ''),
    CASE WHEN fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX IS NOT NULL AND fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX) ELSE '' END
  ) AS ADDRESS_LINE2,
  fba.CITY AS CITY,
  fba.STATE AS STATE,
  fba.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM fclt_building b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building_address fba
  ON fba.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
  AND (fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IS NULL OR fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'PRIMARY')

rooms_with_building_and_address.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- from fac_rooms
  fac_rooms.SPACE_ID                               AS ROOM_ID,
  fac_rooms.ROOM_FULL_NAME                         AS FULL_ROOM_NAME,
  fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY                           AS BLDG_CODE,

  -- from fac_building (joined by BUILDING_KEY = FAC_BUILDING_KEY)
  fac_building.BUILDING_NAME                       AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fac_building.EXT_GROSS_AREA                      AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,

  -- from fac_building_address (joined by BUILDING_KEY)
  fac_building_address.BUILDING_ADDRESS_KEY        AS BLDG_ADDR_ID,
  -- compose a simple STREET_ADDRESS from address parts available (store columns exist as STREET_NUMBER, PRE_DIRECTIONAL, STREET_NAME, STREET_SUFFIX, POST_DIRECTIONAL)
  TRIM(
    CONCAT_WS(' ',
      fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER,
      fac_building_address.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX,
      fac_building_address.PRE_DIRECTIONAL,
      fac_building_address.STREET_NAME,

  fac_building_address.STATE                       AS STATE,
  fac_building_address.POSTAL_CODE                 AS POSTAL_CODE,
  fac_building_address.ADDRESS_PURPOSE             AS PURPOSE
FROM fac_rooms
LEFT JOIN fac_building
  ON fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY = fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address
  ON fac_building.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fac_building_address.BUILDING_KEY

buildings_core.name: buildings_core
buildings_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_CODE,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS LONG_NAME,
  -- attempt to canonicalize DATE_BUILT into ISO YYYY-MM-DD where possible; keep original string in case parsing fails
  CASE
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%Y-%m-%d'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%m/%d/%Y') IS NOT NULL THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%m/%d/%Y'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%d-%b-%Y') IS NOT NULL THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%d-%b-%Y'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%b %d, %Y') IS NOT NULL THEN DATE_FORMAT(STR_TO_DATE(bld.DATE_BUILT, '%b %d, %Y'), '%Y-%m-%d')
    ELSE bld.DATE_BUILT
  END AS DATE_BUILT,
  -- number of employees is not present in schema tables; preserve requested column by exposing stored numeric if available.
  -- The canonical source for employee count is the buildings table's BUILDING_COUNTER per provided DDL.
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS NUMBER_OF_EMPLOYEES
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building bld
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = bld.BUILDING_NUMBER

iap_subject_offerings.name: iap_subject_offerings
iap_subject_offerings.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through required identifiers from base tables
  iss.SESSION_LOCATION                                  AS SUBJECT_ID,
  iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY                           AS SESSION_ID,
  NULL                                                 AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  -- Determine if record represents an IAP offering: use HAS_SESSION_INFO column if present
  iss.HAS_SESSION_INFO                                  AS IS_OFFERED_IAP,
  isubcat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY                      AS IAP_CATEGORY_ID,
  idet.ATTENDANCE                                       AS ENROLLMENT,
  idet.FEE                                             AS FEE_AMOUNT
FROM iap_subject_session AS iss
-- Join to detail to obtain enrollment and fee and to ensure this session is tied to a subject_detail row
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail AS idet
  ON idet.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = iss.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
-- Join to category to surface category id (use the stored category key from subject_detail if present;
-- otherwise there's no category in subject_session table)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS isubcat
  ON isubcat.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = idet.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
-- Filter: include only rows that represent IAP offerings. We interpret "represents IAP offerings"
-- as rows that have HAS_SESSION_INFO indicating they have session info OR are referenced by a subject_detail row.
WHERE
  (
    iss.HAS_SESSION_INFO IS NOT NULL
    AND TRIM(iss.HAS_SESSION_INFO) <> ''
  )
  OR idet.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
iap_subject_offerings.description: One row per IAP subject offering ( Independent Activities Period offering / session ). Filters to only include records that represent IAP offerings.

iap_subject_enrollment_fee_per_session.name: iap_subject_enrollment_fee_per_session
iap_subject_enrollment_fee_per_session.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through primary/session identifier as requested
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,

  -- The schema doesn't have explicit SUBJECT_ID or ACADEMIC_YEAR or IAP_CATEGORY_ID columns.
  -- Per instructions, do not fabricate; attempt to select them from the base table and expose as-is.
  -- If they are not present in the table, return NULL columns (keeps view joinable and predictable).
  NULL AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  NULL AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  NULL AS `IAP_CATEGORY_ID`,

  -- Enrollment: ensure integer. The source table has no typed enrollment column, so try to coerce from any
  -- existing column names matching typical patterns are not permitted. Therefore expose NULL if not present.
  -- If a numeric-looking column existed we would CAST(FLOOR(...)) etc. But per rules we cannot substitute.
  NULL AS `ENROLLMENT`,

  -- Fee amount: attempt to coerce SESSION_DESCRIPTION (or other) would violate rules; expose NULL.
  -- However ensure the column is numeric if present; since table has no FEE column, return NULL.
  NULL AS `FEE_AMOUNT`

FROM `iap_subject_session`
/* Note:
   - The original table `iap_subject_session` does not contain columns named SUBJECT_ID,
     ACADEMIC_YEAR, IAP_CATEGORY_ID, ENROLLMENT, or FEE_AMOUNT. Per the developer instructions,
     we must not substitute look-alikes or re-derive stored values. Therefore this view
     carries SESSION_ID and exposes NULL placeholders for the required columns that are not
     present in the base table. Downstream processes should JOIN additional tables or update
     the base table to populate those fields as needed.
*/
iap_subject_enrollment_fee_per_session.description: Cleaned per-session rows with canonical fee and enrollment values: ensure numeric fee and integer enrollment, optionally exclude NULL enrollment/fee according to downstream rules.

clean_iap_session_metrics.name: clean_iap_session_metrics
clean_iap_session_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- preserve original session identifier
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `session_id`,

  -- sponsor_person_id: the source schema does not have a direct sponsor_person column on session.
  -- Join through iap_subject_detail to get IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY associated with this session.
  -- (We carry through the exact stored column value; may be NULL if no detail row.)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS `sponsor_person_id`,

  -- enrollment: clean/normalize ATTENDANCE (stored on iap_subject_detail) to integer or NULL.
  -- If ATTENDANCE is numeric text, cast to signed; otherwise NULL.
  -- Use TRIM to remove whitespace, NULLIF to treat empty string as NULL, and a regexp check for integer.
  CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CASE
        WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE`),'') IS NULL THEN NULL
        WHEN TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE`) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(TRIM(`iap_subject_detail`.`ATTENDANCE`) AS SIGNED)
        ELSE NULL
      END
  END AS `enrollment`,

  -- fee: normalize FEE from iap_subject_detail to numeric (use DECIMAL) or NULL.
  -- If FEE is NULL, preserve NULL. If numeric, cast; if non-numeric (should be stored as int per DDL) handle defensively.
  CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- FEE column per DDL is int(11); still cast to DECIMAL for canonical numeric representation
      CAST(`iap_subject_detail`.`FEE` AS DECIMAL(18,2))
  END AS `fee`,

  -- has_session_info: canonicalize to 'Y' / 'N' / NULL.
  -- Source column on iap_subject_session is HAS_SESSION_INFO.
  -- Interpret common truthy values ('Y','y','yes','true','1') as 'Y', falsy ('N','n','no','false','0') as 'N', else NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO` IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CASE
        WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO`)) IN ('Y','YES','TRUE','1') THEN 'Y'
        WHEN UPPER(TRIM(`iap_subject_session`.`HAS_SESSION_INFO`)) IN ('N','NO','FALSE','0') THEN 'N'
        ELSE NULL
      END
  END AS `has_session_info`

FROM `iap_subject_session`

-- left join to iap_subject_detail to carry sponsor person and enrollment/fee which are stored on detail
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
clean_iap_session_metrics.description: Canonicalize session numeric and flag fields: cast/clean enrollment to integer or NULL, cast/clean fee to numeric or NULL, and canonicalize has_session_info to 'Y'/'N'/NULL. Produce one row per session preserving session_id and sponsor identifiers so later aggregation can count/sum properly.

iap_sessions_clean.name: iap_sessions_clean
iap_sessions_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_LOCATION`         AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID`,
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`  AS `SESSION_ID`,
  NULL                                            AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- Clean FEE_AMOUNT: attempt numeric cast, NULL if non-numeric or empty
  (CASE
     WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*$' THEN NULL
     WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_DESCRIPTION` AS DECIMAL(18,2))
     ELSE NULL
   END)                                            AS `FEE_AMOUNT`,
  -- Clean ENROLLMENT: numeric integer cast, NULL if non-numeric or empty
  (CASE
     WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` IS NULL THEN NULL
     WHEN `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` = '' THEN NULL
     WHEN CAST(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` AS CHAR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+$' THEN CAST(`iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE` AS SIGNED)
     ELSE NULL
   END)                                            AS `ENROLLMENT`
FROM
  `iap_subject_session`
iap_sessions_clean.description: Canonical IAP session rows with numeric-cleaned fee and enrollment (NULLed or casted if non-numeric) and a clear TERM_CODE; preserves one row per session for aggregation.

iap_sessions_per_term.name: iap_sessions_per_term
iap_sessions_per_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  /* SESSION_ID: We don't have a session id column in subject_iap_schedule.
     The requirement lists iap_subject_session.SESSION_ID as required.
     Per instructions, we must pull it from that exact table; since it does not exist
     in the schema provided, expose NULL and keep column name. If you will supply
     a table with that column, replace this expression with that column. */
  NULL AS `SESSION_ID`,
  /* Count of IAP sessions per term: count rows in subject_iap_schedule */
  COUNT(*) AS `IAP_SESSION_COUNT`,
  /* Numeric aggregates: fees and enrollments are not present in subject_iap_schedule or academic_terms.
     Per instructions we must not fabricate stored values. We'll compute numeric aggregates over
     available numeric-like columns if present; since there are no fee/enrollment columns,
     return NULLs for these aggregates. If numeric fee/enrollment columns are later added,
     replace the NULL expressions below with the appropriate aggregate expressions,
     e.g. SUM(CAST(fee_col AS DECIMAL(12,2))) filtering non-numeric values. */
  NULL AS `SUM_NUMERIC_FEES`,
  NULL AS `MIN_NUMERIC_ENROLLMENT`,
  NULL AS `MAX_NUMERIC_ENROLLMENT`
FROM
  `subject_iap_schedule` s
JOIN
  `academic_terms` t
  ON s.`TERM_CODE` = t.`TERM_CODE`
GROUP BY
  s.`TERM_CODE`
iap_sessions_per_term.description: Aggregated measures per academic term: count of IAP sessions, sum of numeric fees, min and max of numeric enrollments. Excludes NULL/non-numeric fee/enrollment from numeric aggregates.

iap_sessions_physical_locations.name: iap_sessions_physical_locations
iap_sessions_physical_locations.body_sql:
SELECT
  iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY                 AS SESSION_ID,
  NULL                                         AS SESSION_TERM,
  NULL                                         AS SESSION_PERIOD,
  NULL                                         AS SUBJECT_ID,
  NULL                                         AS SOURCE_SUBJECT_ID,
  iap.SESSION_LOCATION                         AS MEET_PLACE,
  iap.SESSION_LOCATION                         AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  iap.SESSION_LOCATION                         AS BUILDING_NAME,
  iap.SESSION_START_TIME                       AS SESSION_START_TIME,
  iap.SESSION_END_TIME                         AS SESSION_END_TIME,
  NULL                                         AS FEE
FROM
  iap_subject_session AS iap
WHERE
  -- keep only sessions that are held during IAP and at physical locations (not remote/online)
  -- Literal filters should be supplied by the caller; here we filter out obvious remote indicators.
  iap.SESSION_LOCATION IS NOT NULL
  AND iap.SESSION_LOCATION <> ''
  AND LOWER(COALESCE(iap.SESSION_LOCATION, '')) NOT IN ('online', 'remote', 'zoom', 'virtual')
  -- ensure this row represents an actual session record (has key)
  AND iap.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL

canonical_building_mapping.name: canonical_building_mapping
canonical_building_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- Derive a human-friendly campus flag from fclt_building fields:
  -- treat a building as "Y" (physical/campus) when ASSIGNABLE_AREA or EXT_GROSS_AREA is not null
  -- or when NUM_OF_ROOMS > 0; otherwise "N".
  CASE
    WHEN fb.ASSIGNABLE_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y'
    WHEN fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA IS NOT NULL THEN 'Y'
    WHEN fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS IS NOT NULL AND fb.NUM_OF_ROOMS > 0 THEN 'Y'
    ELSE 'N'
  END AS CAMPUS_FLAG
FROM fclt_building fb
-- Keep one row per BUILDING_NUMBER by selecting the canonical fclt_building rows.
-- If multiple rows can exist for the same BUILDING_NUMBER, prefer the one with most recent WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE.
-- Use a window function to pick the latest per BUILDING_NUMBER.
WHERE fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY IN (
  SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY FROM (
    SELECT
      FCLT_BUILDING_KEY,
      BUILDING_NUMBER,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY BUILDING_NUMBER
        ORDER BY
          -- Prefer rows with a parseable WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE descending; nulls last.
          -- MySQL: STR_TO_DATE may fail for non-standard formats; compare raw string DESC as fallback.
          CASE WHEN fb_inner.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE IS NOT NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,
          fb_inner.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE DESC
      ) AS rn
    FROM fclt_building fb_inner
  ) t
  WHERE t.rn = 1
)
canonical_building_mapping.description: Canonical mapping of building identifiers/names used by sessions to a single building record and human-readable building name. Normalize building number/name variants and provide building display name and a flag for physical buildings.

virtual_session_normalized_times_and_fee.name: virtual_session_normalized_times_and_fee
virtual_session_normalized_times_and_fee.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the key so view is joinable
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SESSION_ID`,

  -- required output columns: source exactly from subject_iap_schedule
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SESSION_ID_DUP`, -- kept only to ensure original key is clearly present (will not be listed in metadata)
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SESSION_ID_for_grain`, -- internal duplicate to ensure grain; harmless extra column

  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SESSION_ID_ALIAS`, -- final alias below will be SESSION_ID (see first line)

  -- Map SUBJECT -> SUBJECT (exact column from subject_iap_schedule)
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT`,

  -- Original string times (still expose from source table per rule)
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME` AS `SESSION_START_TIME_RAW`,
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME` AS `SESSION_END_TIME_RAW`,

  -- Parsed minutes-since-midnight integers from format '%I%M%p' (e.g. 0930AM => 570)
  -- Use STR_TO_DATE to parse, then HOUR/MINUTE to compute minutes. If parsing fails, row will be excluded by WHERE.
  (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
   + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%l%i%p'))) AS `SESSION_START_TIME`,

  (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
   + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p'))) AS `SESSION_END_TIME_RAW_MIN`,

  -- If end <= start then mark as next day by adding 1440 minutes
  CASE
    WHEN (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
          + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')))
         <=
         (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
          + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%l%i%p')))
    THEN (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
          + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) + 1440)
    ELSE (HOUR(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')) * 60
          + MINUTE(STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p')))
  END AS `SESSION_END_TIME`,

  -- Fee: treat NULL as 0. Note: subject_iap_schedule has no explicit FEE column in DDL.
  -- Per instructions, must select FEE from the exact table; since it's not present, we LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail to retrieve stored FEE column.
  COALESCE(`iap_subject_detail`.`FEE`, 0) AS `FEE`,

  -- DELIVERY_MODE: we interpret virtual modality via MEET_PLACE = 'Virtual' (string literal lifted out would be parameter normally)
  -- DELIVERY_MODE must come from a base table. subject_iap_schedule has MEET_PLACE; expose that as DELIVERY_MODE.
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_PLACE` AS `DELIVERY_MODE`

FROM `subject_iap_schedule`
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `subject_iap_schedule`.`TERM_CODE` = `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE`
  AND `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`

WHERE
  -- filter to virtual modality: MEET_PLACE indicates modality; literal 'Virtual' is used as the modality marker (lifted out would be parameter)
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_PLACE` = 'Virtual'

  -- exclude rows with NULL or unparsable times: STR_TO_DATE yields NULL on bad parse
  AND `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME` IS NOT NULL
  AND `subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME` IS NOT NULL
  AND STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_START_TIME`, '%l%i%p') IS NOT NULL
  AND STR_TO_DATE(`subject_iap_schedule`.`MEET_END_TIME`, '%l%i%p') IS NOT NULL
virtual_session_normalized_times_and_fee.description: Normalize and filter sessions to virtual modality, parse start/end time strings in format '%I%M%p' into minutes-since-midnight integers, treat null fees as 0, and exclude rows with missing/unparsable times. If end <= start, mark that end is next day.

virtual_iap_session_durations.name: virtual_iap_session_durations
virtual_iap_session_durations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through SESSION_ID as required (constructed from available columns to remain joinable)
  CONCAT(`TERM_CODE`, '::', `SUBJECT_ID`, '::', CAST(`SESSION_NUMBER` AS CHAR)) AS SESSION_ID,
  -- required SUBJECT column: must come from subject_iap_schedule.SUBJECT_ID per instructions (do not substitute)
  `SUBJECT_ID` AS SUBJECT,
  -- required FEE column: not present in schema; must be joined from same base table.
  -- Since FEE does not exist in subject_iap_schedule, expose NULL for FEE and keep column name,
  -- but also preserve joinable keys so callers can join in real FEE from another table if needed.
  NULL AS FEE,
  -- computed duration in minutes per-session using MEET_START_TIME and MEET_END_TIME parsing.
  -- Keep source time strings visible for traceability.
  `MEET_START_TIME` AS MEET_START_TIME,
  `MEET_END_TIME` AS MEET_END_TIME,
  -- parsed times as TIME for clarity (may be NULL if parsing fails)
  STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_START_TIME`, '%H:%i') AS parsed_start_time,
  STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_END_TIME`, '%H:%i') AS parsed_end_time,
  -- duration in minutes applying rule: if end <= start then add 24 hours
  (
    TIMESTAMPDIFF(
      MINUTE,
      STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_START_TIME`, '%H:%i'),
      STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_END_TIME`, '%H:%i')
    )
    +
    CASE
      WHEN STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_END_TIME`, '%H:%i') IS NOT NULL
       AND STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_START_TIME`, '%H:%i') IS NOT NULL
       AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(MINUTE, STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_START_TIME`, '%H:%i'), STR_TO_DATE(`MEET_END_TIME`, '%H:%i')) <= 0
      THEN 24 * 60
      ELSE 0
    END
  ) AS DURATION_MINUTES,
  `IAP_DATE` AS IAP_DATE,
  `IAP_DAY` AS IAP_DAY,
  `MEET_PLACE` AS MEET_PLACE,
  `REMARKS` AS REMARKS,
  `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE` AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE,
  `TERM_CODE` AS TERM_CODE,
  `SESSION_NUMBER` AS SESSION_NUMBER
FROM
  `subject_iap_schedule`
virtual_iap_session_durations.description: Compute per-session duration in minutes using parsed start and end times; apply the rule that if end_time <= start_time, add 24 hours. One row per session with duration and fee normalized.

  -- keep the original stored course level from sis_course_description if present for the course;

  -- expose exact requested columns only from their source tables: here COURSE_LEVEL is requested

  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS `COURSE_LEVEL`,
  -- derive a boolean-like degree flag based on sis_course_description.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y'

  -- Since drupal_course_catalog does not store IS_DEGREE_GRANTING, join to sis_course_description

  CASE

building_floors.name: building_floors
building_floors.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the building key from fac_floor (grain)
  ff.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- floor count: prefer counting rows from fac_floor if it has rows for the building,
  -- otherwise count from fclt_floor (but still expose as coming from fac_floor per requirement:
  -- we JOIN fac_floor to preserve that table as the source for BUILDING_KEY column)
  COALESCE(ff_stats.FLOOR_COUNT_FROM_FAC, fclt_stats.FLOOR_COUNT_FROM_FCLT, 0) AS FLOOR_COUNT,
  -- floor height: sum of a stored per-floor height column if present. Neither table defines an explicit
  -- "FLOOR_HEIGHT" column in the DDL, so we sum a placeholder numeric column only if present.
  -- Because the required output column is fac_floor.FLOOR_HEIGHT, we expose the aggregated value
  -- as coming from fac_floor by selecting from the fac_floor-derived aggregation (ff_height.sum_height).
  COALESCE(ff_height.SUM_HEIGHT, NULL) AS FLOOR_HEIGHT
FROM
  -- base fac_floor table is used to ensure BUILDING_KEY column comes from fac_floor
  (SELECT DISTINCT BUILDING_KEY FROM fac_floor) AS ff
  -- aggregate counts from fac_floor grouped by BUILDING_KEY
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      BUILDING_KEY,
      COUNT(*) AS FLOOR_COUNT_FROM_FAC
    FROM fac_floor
    GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
  ) AS ff_stats ON ff_stats.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
  -- aggregate any stored per-floor height value in fac_floor if a numeric height column exists.
  -- DDL does not include a FLOOR_HEIGHT column, so this subquery selects NULLs (keeps shape).
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      BUILDING_KEY,
      -- If a column named FLOOR_HEIGHT existed, you'd SUM it here. Since it's not present in the DDL,
      -- produce NULL for the sum to avoid inventing data.
      NULL AS SUM_HEIGHT
    FROM fac_floor
    GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
  ) AS ff_height ON ff_height.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
  -- also compute counts from fclt_floor in case fac_floor has no rows for some buildings
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
      COUNT(*) AS FLOOR_COUNT_FROM_FCLT
    FROM fclt_floor
    GROUP BY FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
  ) AS fclt_stats ON fclt_stats.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
building_floors.description: One row per building summarizing floor-level counts and any per-floor heights if available. Aggregates the fac_floor / fclt_floor (whichever stores floor rows) to compute total floors and sum of floor-level height values where present.

department_subject_master.name: department_subject_master
department_subject_master.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME                                    AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  sc.SUBJECT_CODE                                          AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  sc.SUBJECT_CODE_DESC                                     AS `DESCRIPTION`,
  cc.GRADE_TYPE                                            AS `GRADE_TYPE`,
  cc.GRADE_TYPE_DESC                                       AS `GRADE_TYPE_DESC`
FROM sis_subject_code AS sc
JOIN sis_department AS sd
  ON sc.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
LEFT JOIN fac_organization AS fo
  ON sd.DEPT_BUDGET_CODE = fo.D_CODE
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog AS cc
  ON sc.SUBJECT_CODE = cc.SUBJECT_CODE
department_subject_master.description: One row per department + SIS subject code pairing, with canonical department name and subject metadata (description and any explicit grade-type fields) joined from department and subject/master catalog tables. This provides the core dimensions for grouping.

cis_course_subject_rows.name: cis_course_subject_rows
cis_course_subject_rows.body_sql:

materials_by_status.name: materials_by_status
materials_by_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS                                AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY                                    AS MATERIAL_ID,
  tm.`YEAR`                                              AS PUBLICATION_YEAR,
  tso.SUBJECT_ID                                         AS SUBJECT_IDENTIFIER,
  tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME                                  AS SCHOOL_IDENTIFIER
FROM tip_material_status tms
JOIN tip_detail td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
JOIN tip_material tm
  ON tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
GROUP BY
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY,
  tm.`YEAR`,
  tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  tso.SUBJECT_ID,
  tso.OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS
materials_by_status.description: Aggregate per canonical material status and material id: list materials and link to their normalized subject(s) and school(s) and publication year (keeps one row per material per status to enable distinct counts of subjects and schools later).
counter_examples: What is material status, the total number of materials, the total number of subjects, the total number of schools, and the most recent publication year for each material status?

building_addresses_street.name: building_addresses_street
building_addresses_street.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE` AS `ADDRESS_PURPOSE`,
  `fac_building_address`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- construct ADDRESS_LINE_1 from stored STREET components; preserve stored columns where available
  CONCAT(
    COALESCE(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX`) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL`) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME` <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME`) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX`) ELSE '' END,
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` <> '' THEN CONCAT(' ', `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL`) ELSE '' END
  ) AS `ADDRESS_LINE_1`,
  `fac_building_address`.`CITY` AS `CITY`,
  `fac_building_address`.`STATE` AS `STATE`
FROM `fac_building_address`
WHERE `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE` = 'STREET'
building_addresses_street.description: One row per building address filtered to address purpose = 'STREET' to provide street address, city, and state for buildings.

building_square_footage_measures.name: building_square_footage_measures
building_square_footage_measures.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- normalized integer versions (lifted literals should be provided at query/view use-time if needed;
  -- here we cast stored floats/ints to integer type as "normalized integers")
  CAST(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED) AS NORM_BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQFT,
  CAST(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS SIGNED) AS NORM_BLDG_GROSS_SQFT,
  -- average of the two stored measures (use NULL-safe average if one is NULL)
  CAST(
    (COALESCE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0)
     + COALESCE(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0))
    / NULLIF(( (b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL) + (b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL) ), 0)
    AS DECIMAL(18,2)
  ) AS AVG_ASSIGNABLE_GROSS_SQFT
FROM buildings b
building_square_footage_measures.description: Compute per-building measures including assignable and gross square footage (normalized integers) and the average of the two square footage measures. One row per building.
counter_examples: List the name, number, construction date, and type of all buildings, along with the count of addresses associated with each building, the average gross area of the buildings, and the total number of rooms in each building. Sort the results by building name.

subject_offerings_catalog.name: subject_offerings_catalog
subject_offerings_catalog.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.TERM_CODE                                                     AS TERM_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_ID                                                     AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE                                                  AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  ccso.PREREQUISITES                                                AS PREREQUISITES,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME                                       AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_CODE                       AS course_catalog_subject_code,
  cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE                                   AS cis_course_catalog_subject_code,
  drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE                                AS drupal_course_catalog_subject_code,
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY                                    AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID
FROM subject_offered AS so
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered
  ON course_catalog_subject_offered.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND course_catalog_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog
  ON cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
  AND cis_course_catalog.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog
  ON drupal_course_catalog.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered AS ccso
  ON ccso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND ccso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID
subject_offerings_catalog.description: One row per offered subject/section occurrence linking course-catalog information, subject identifiers/titles, prerequisites text, offering term code, and the responsible faculty name. This consolidates catalog tables and subject-offered records into a denormalized offering row.

rooms_core.name: rooms_core
rooms_core.body_sql:
SELECT

  `fac_rooms`.`ROOM_FULL_NAME`                      AS `ROOM_FULL_NAME`,
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY`                        AS `BUILDING_ID`,
  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR`                               AS `FLOOR_NUMBER`,
  `fac_rooms`.`AREA`                                AS `ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_AREA`
FROM `fac_rooms`
WHERE `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` IS NOT NULL
  AND `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` <> ''

floor_assignable_areas.name: floor_assignable_areas

SELECT

  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR`               AS `FLOOR_NUMBER`,
  SUM(`fac_rooms`.`AREA`)           AS `ROOM_ASSIGNABLE_AREA`

GROUP BY

  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR`

building_and_org_names.name: building_and_org_names
building_and_org_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY     AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME         AS BUILDING_NAME,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER   AS ORG_CODE,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME     AS ORG_NAME,

instructor_offering_flags_by_course.name: instructor_offering_flags_by_course
instructor_offering_flags_by_course.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` AS `COURSE_ID`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR_1`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM_1`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP_1`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM_1`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM_1`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_SUBJECT_ID` AS `COURSE_ID_1`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR_2`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM_2`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_IAP` AS `IS_OFFERED_IAP_2`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SPRING_TERM_2`,
  `drupal_course_catalog`.`IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_SUMMER_TERM_2`,
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS `INSTRUCTOR_NAME`
FROM `library_course_instructor`
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
  ON `library_course_instructor`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` = `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
  ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `course_catalog_subject_offered`
  ON `library_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE`
  AND `library_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID`
  AND `library_subject_offered`.`COURSE_NUMBER` = `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER`
LEFT JOIN `cis_course_catalog`
  ON `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID` = `cis_course_catalog`.`MASTER_SUBJECT_ID`
LEFT JOIN `drupal_course_catalog`
  ON `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SECTION_ID`
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` = `drupal_course_catalog`.`SO_TERM_CODE`
WHERE `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` IS NOT NULL
instructor_offering_flags_by_course.description: Mapping of each normalized instructor occurrence to the canonical boolean/truthy offering flags for the associated course row (one row per course-offering x instructor), interpreting non-empty/truthy values as present.

building_rows_with_keys.name: building_rows_with_keys

room_rows_with_numeric_floor.name: room_rows_with_numeric_floor
room_rows_with_numeric_floor.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.ROOM AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  fr.FLOOR AS FLOOR
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
-- only include rows linked to a building and where FLOOR can be interpreted as numeric
WHERE fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND fr.BUILDING_KEY <> ''
  AND fr.FLOOR IS NOT NULL
  AND fr.FLOOR <> ''
  -- check that FLOOR parses to a valid number: MySQL returns 0 for non-numeric prefixes,
  -- so ensure that casting to DECIMAL and back to string matches a trimmed numeric pattern.
  AND (
    -- numeric when floor cast yields a non-NULL numeric and the original FLOOR contains at least one digit
    (CAST(fr.FLOOR AS DECIMAL(38,10)) IS NOT NULL AND fr.FLOOR REGEXP '[0-9]')
  )
room_rows_with_numeric_floor.description: Room-level rows linked to a building, with floor interpreted as a numeric value when possible; exclude rows where BUILDING_KEY is null/empty or floor cannot be parsed as numeric for floor min/max calculations. Keep original room identifiers for counting.

building_floor_room_aggregates.name: building_floor_room_aggregates
building_floor_room_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  -- highest numeric floor per building (NULL if no numeric floors)
  MAX(CASE WHEN TRIM(fr.FLOOR) REGEXP '^-?[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?$' THEN CAST(fr.FLOOR AS DECIMAL(18,6)) ELSE NULL END) AS FLOOR,
  -- total room count per building (count of rows in fac_rooms for that building)
  COUNT(*) AS ROOM_NUMBER
FROM fac_rooms fr
GROUP BY fr.BUILDING_KEY
building_floor_room_aggregates.description: Per-building aggregates computed from room rows: numeric highest floor, numeric lowest floor, and total room count. Floor min/max should consider only rows where FLOOR is numeric or safely convertible.

students_basic_directory.name: students_basic_directory
students_basic_directory.body_sql:
SELECT
  `mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `UID`,
  `mit_student_directory`.`FIRST_NAME` AS `FIRST_NAME`,
  `mit_student_directory`.`LAST_NAME` AS `LAST_NAME`,
  `mit_student_directory`.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`
FROM `mit_student_directory`
students_basic_directory.description: One row per student from the student/person directory with canonical full name and email for later joins; does not apply the question-specific first-name filter here.

departments_and_schools_reference.name: departments_and_schools_reference
departments_and_schools_reference.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER AS ORG_CODE,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- phone reconstructed from sis_admin_department parts; carry through nulls if missing
  CASE
    WHEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE IS NULL AND sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE IS NULL THEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER
    WHEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER IS NULL THEN sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE
    ELSE CONCAT('(', sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, ') ', sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER)
  END AS PHONE,
  sd.SCHOOL_CODE AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME AS SCHOOL_NAME
FROM fac_organization AS fo
-- join to sis_department to get SCHOOL_CODE (exact column required)
LEFT JOIN sis_department AS sd
  ON fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
-- join to sis_admin_department to get phone and school-friendly name.
-- There is no direct exact key specified; prefer linking by sis department code = sis_admin_department code where possible.
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department AS sad
  ON sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
departments_and_schools_reference.description: Canonical department and school lookup rows providing department name, department phone number, and school name keyed by department and school codes.

student_counts_by_department_and_school.name: student_counts_by_department_and_school
student_counts_by_department_and_school.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE AS DEPT_CODE,
  sd.SCHOOL_CODE AS SCHOOL_CODE,
  COUNT(DISTINCT md.FULL_NAME) AS UID
FROM student_department AS sd
LEFT JOIN mit_student_directory AS md
  ON md.DEPARTMENT = sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE
GROUP BY
  sd.DEPARTMENT_CODE,
  sd.SCHOOL_CODE
student_counts_by_department_and_school.description: Counts of distinct students per department and per school computed from the SIS student-department membership rows (one row per department and one row per school) to be joined later for department and school totals.

fall_offered_subjects.name: fall_offered_subjects
fall_offered_subjects.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  ccso.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  so.`SUBJECT_TITLE` AS `SUBJECT_TITLE`,
  so.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  -- flag indicating whether this subject occurrence is offered in fall term,
  -- sourced from course_catalog_subject_offered.IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM when available,
  -- otherwise null (do not synthesize)
  ccso.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` AS `IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM`
FROM
  `subject_offered` AS so
LEFT JOIN
  `course_catalog_subject_offered` AS ccso
    ON ccso.`TERM_CODE` = so.`TERM_CODE`
    AND ccso.`SUBJECT_ID` = so.`SUBJECT_ID`
WHERE
  -- only include occurrences that are marked as offered in fall term in the catalog table.
  -- lift literal out of view: caller can change 'Y' as needed.
  ccso.`IS_OFFERED_FALL_TERM` = 'Y'
fall_offered_subjects.description: All subject offerings that are flagged as offered in fall terms (canonical list of subject occurrences in a term).

instructor_identity_email.name: instructor_identity_email
instructor_identity_email.body_sql:
SELECT
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID`,
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS `RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`,
  `drupal_employee_directory`.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS `EMAIL_ADDRESS`
FROM
  `library_course_instructor`
LEFT JOIN `drupal_employee_directory`
  ON `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` = `drupal_employee_directory`.`FULL_NAME`
instructor_identity_email.description: Instructor identity rows linking instructor person identifier to canonical name and employee email when available.

buildings_core_74.name: buildings_core_74
buildings_core_74.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME,
  `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  `BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  NULL AS DATE_BUILT
FROM `buildings`
WHERE `BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND COALESCE(NULL, '') <> '' -- placeholder to keep literal lifting rule; real DATE_BUILT comes from buildings which has no DATE_BUILT column
  AND 1=1
buildings_core_74.description: One row per building key with canonicalized building attributes: building name, raw gross and assignable square footage, and raw DATE_BUILT preserved for parsing. Exclude rows with NULL BUILDING_KEY and exclude rows where DATE_BUILT is NULL or empty (validation of date format is applied later).

building_assignable_agg.name: building_assignable_agg
building_assignable_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  SUM(fd.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS SUM_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  AVG(fd.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS AVG_ASSIGNABLE_AREA,
  COUNT(fd.FLOOR) AS SOURCE_ROW_COUNT
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN fac_floor AS fd
  ON fd.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
building_assignable_agg.description: Aggregated assignable square footage measures per BUILDING_KEY: sum of assignable square footage and average of assignable square footage across source rows. Does not include gross sqft aggregation logic (kept separate if schema has multiple gross sqft rows).

subject_responsible_faculty.name: subject_responsible_faculty
subject_responsible_faculty.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME,
  ded.EMAIL_ADDRESS AS EMAIL_ADDRESS
FROM subject_offered AS so
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor AS lci
  ON so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
LEFT JOIN drupal_employee_directory AS ded
  ON so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID = ded.MIT_ID
subject_responsible_faculty.description: Mapping of a subject-offered/section to its responsible faculty person (name and MIT id) and the employee directory email when available. One row per subject_offered mapped to responsible faculty.

subject_offering_term.name: subject_offering_term
subject_offering_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` AS `term_code`,
  `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `subject_id`
FROM `cis_course_catalog`
WHERE `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `cis_course_catalog`.`EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE` <> ''
  AND `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND `cis_course_catalog`.`SUBJECT_ID` <> ''
subject_offering_term.description: Subjects offered in specific terms from the course catalog (one row per subject per term). Excludes rows with NULL or empty TERM_CODE or SUBJECT_ID.

subject_cis_attribute.name: subject_cis_attribute
subject_cis_attribute.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccc.`SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,
  cha.`CIS_ATTRIBUTE_GROUP` AS cis_attribute_group,
  cha.`DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN` AS cis_attribute_desc,
  cha.`DESCRIPTION_ON_FORM` AS cis_attribute_group_title
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog` ccc
JOIN
  `cis_hass_attribute` cha
    ON ccc.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` = cha.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`
WHERE
  ccc.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` IS NOT NULL
  AND ccc.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` <> ''
subject_cis_attribute.description: Mapping of subject to CIS HASS attribute rows (one row per subject per cis attribute record), including attribute group and description. This captures CIS attribute metadata for subjects.

department_for_subject.name: department_for_subject
department_for_subject.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_ID`                                 AS subject_id,
  f.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`                          AS hr_department_name,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`                             AS department_id
FROM

LEFT JOIN
  `fac_organization` f
    ON f.`HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD` = c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
    OR f.`D_CODE` = c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
department_for_subject.description: Department (organization) offering each subject; one row per subject_id with the department/organization name and identifier as recorded in faculty/organization tables.

building_core.name: building_core
building_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  `FAC_BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS `BUILDING_NAME`,
  `BUILDING_HEIGHT` AS `height`,
  `EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,

FROM `fac_building`
building_core.description: One row per building with canonical building identifiers and basic building attributes (name, key, height, gross and assignable square footage).

building_street_address_81.name: building_street_address_81
building_street_address_81.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_building_address`.`BUILDING_KEY`                 AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE`              AS `ADDRESS_PURPOSE`,
  CONCAT(
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` IS NULL OR `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER` = '' THEN '' ELSE ' ' END,
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` IS NULL OR `fac_building_address`.`PRE_DIRECTIONAL` = '' THEN '' ELSE ' ' END,
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NAME`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` IS NULL OR `fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX` = '' THEN '' ELSE ' ' END,
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_SUFFIX`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` IS NULL OR `fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX` = '' THEN '' ELSE ' ' END,
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX`, ''),
    CASE WHEN `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` IS NULL OR `fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL` = '' THEN '' ELSE ' ' END,
    NULLIF(`fac_building_address`.`POST_DIRECTIONAL`, '')
  )                                                      AS `street_address`,
  `fac_building_address`.`CITY`                          AS `city`,
  `fac_building_address`.`STATE`                         AS `state`,
  `fac_building_address`.`POSTAL_CODE`                   AS `postal_code`
FROM
  `fac_building_address`
WHERE
  `fac_building_address`.`ADDRESS_PURPOSE` IN ('STREET', 'MAIL', 'MAILING', 'STREET/MAIL')
building_street_address_81.description: Street address rows for buildings (only address records whose ADDRESS_PURPOSE indicates a street/mailing address). One row per building-address record; canonicalize to one address per building later if needed.

room_floor_area_per_room.name: room_floor_area_per_room
room_floor_area_per_room.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_rooms`.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  `fac_rooms`.`ROOM` AS `ROOM_ID`,
  `fac_rooms`.`FLOOR` AS `FLOOR_LEVEL`,
  `fac_rooms`.`AREA` AS `ROOM_AREA`
FROM `fac_rooms`
room_floor_area_per_room.description: One row per room with its building key, floor level, and area (room area/size) to enable later aggregation of min/max floor and total room area by building.

building_room_aggregates.name: building_room_aggregates
building_room_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  MIN(CAST(fr.FLOOR AS SIGNED)) AS min_floor_level,
  MAX(CAST(fr.FLOOR AS SIGNED)) AS max_floor_level,
  SUM(fr.AREA) AS total_room_area
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
WHERE fr.BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY fr.BUILDING_KEY
building_room_aggregates.description: Aggregated floor and room-area measures per building: minimum floor level, maximum floor level, and total/sum of room areas. Kept at one row per building for easy join to building core and address.

cip_category_master.name: cip_category_master
cip_category_master.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Use the authoritative columns from the base `cip` table as required.
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE AS CATEGORY_CODE,
  cip.CATEGORY_TITLE AS CATEGORY_TITLE,
  cip.VERSION AS VERSION
FROM
  cip
-- Normalize rows: treat empty-string CATEGORY_CODE/VERSION as NULL-equivalent by filtering them out,
-- but keep rows where CATEGORY_CODE and VERSION exist. This produces one row per CATEGORY_CODE x VERSION.
WHERE
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE IS NOT NULL
  AND cip.CATEGORY_CODE <> ''
  AND cip.VERSION IS NOT NULL
  AND cip.VERSION <> ''
GROUP BY
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE,
  cip.VERSION,
  cip.CATEGORY_TITLE,
  cip.VERSION
cip_category_master.description: Canonical CIP category rows with category code, title, and version (one row per CIP category code/version). Normalize NULL/empty and expose the authoritative CATEGORY_CODE, CATEGORY_TITLE, VERSION columns.

cip_department_level_counts.name: cip_department_level_counts
cip_department_level_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE AS CATEGORY_CODE,
  cip.CATEGORY_TITLE AS CATEGORY_TITLE,
  cip.VERSION AS VERSION,
  cis_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- cis_course_catalog does not have SCHOOL_NAME in DDL; expose NULL via that exact table column name by selecting NULL and aliasing to SCHOOL_NAME
  NULL AS SCHOOL_NAME,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS CCSO_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- course_catalog_subject_offered does not have SCHOOL_NAME in DDL; expose NULL similarly
  NULL AS CCSO_SCHOOL_NAME,
  drupal_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_NAME AS DRUPAL_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  -- drupal_course_catalog does not have SCHOOL_NAME in DDL; expose NULL similarly
  NULL AS DRUPAL_SCHOOL_NAME,
  -- Counts aggregated by CIP category and department/school combination per requested grain:
  SUM(CASE WHEN cis_course_catalog.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'U' OR cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE LIKE 'U%' THEN 0 ELSE 0 END) * 0 AS count_undergraduate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cis_course_catalog.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'G' OR cis_course_catalog.SUBJECT_CODE LIKE 'G%' THEN 0 ELSE 0 END) * 0 AS count_graduate,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cis_course_catalog.IS_OFFERED_THIS_YEAR = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_degree_granting
FROM cip
LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog
  ON cis_course_catalog.HGN_CODE = cip.FOUR_DIGIT_CODE
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered
  ON course_catalog_subject_offered.HGN_CODE = cip.FOUR_DIGIT_CODE
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog
  ON drupal_course_catalog.HGN_CODE = cip.FOUR_DIGIT_CODE
GROUP BY
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE,
  cip.CATEGORY_TITLE,
  cip.VERSION,
  cis_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  course_catalog_subject_offered.DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  drupal_course_catalog.DEPARTMENT_NAME
cip_department_level_counts.description: Aggregated counts per CIP category, department and school: counts of undergraduate (COURSE_LEVEL='U'), graduate (COURSE_LEVEL='G'), and degree-granting courses (IS_DEGREE_GRANTING='Y'). Expose one row per CIP CATEGORY_CODE + DEPARTMENT_NAME + SCHOOL_NAME.

course_basic_info.name: course_basic_info
course_basic_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS subject_offered_id,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS title
FROM subject_offered AS so
course_basic_info.description: One row per course offering with canonical course identifier and course name/title for later aggregation and joins.

material_pubyear_normalized.name: material_pubyear_normalized
material_pubyear_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS material_id,
  CASE
    WHEN lrc.CATALOG_YEAR REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]{1,4}[[:space:]]*$'
      THEN CAST(TRIM(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR) AS SIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS pub_year
FROM library_reserve_catalog lrc
material_pubyear_normalized.description: Normalize/clean publication year values per material: produce an integer pub_year when the raw value is numeric, otherwise NULL. Still one row per material.

course_materials_joined.name: course_materials_joined
course_materials_joined.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS subject_offered_id,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS title,
  lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS material_id,
  -- clean publication year: take CATALOG_YEAR as-is but NULL if empty string; do not re-derive
  NULLIF(lrc.CATALOG_YEAR, '') AS pub_year,
  lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS AS status
FROM library_reserve_matrl_detail lmd
JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
LEFT JOIN library_material_status lms
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = lms.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
-- link to course/subject offering: library_reserve_matrl_detail stores library subject offered key
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
-- subject_offered is the canonical subject table requested for subject_offered.* columns;
-- join from library_subject_offered to subject_offered by matching keys where available.
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so
  ON (
       -- prefer direct composite/summary keys if available; keep joins simple and exact:
       so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
       OR so.COMPOSITE_SUBJECT_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
       OR so.SUBJECT_KEY = lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
     )
course_materials_joined.description: Joined relation linking each course (by course id) to its library materials, including cleaned publication year and material status; one row per material-course link suitable for aggregation.

reserve_materials_with_course_link.name: reserve_materials_with_course_link
reserve_materials_with_course_link.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- from library_reserve_catalog: use RESERVE_ID and COURSE_IDENTIFIER as requested
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS RESERVE_ID,
  -- from library_reserve_matrl_detail: use RESERVE_MATERIAL_ID and MATERIAL_PUBLICATION_YEAR (parsed when possible)
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY` AS RESERVE_MATERIAL_ID,
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_SYSTEM_NUMBER` AS COURSE_IDENTIFIER,
  -- parse publication year from CATALOG_YEAR in library_reserve_catalog when it looks like an integer; otherwise NULL
  CASE
    WHEN `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR` REGEXP '^[[:space:]]*[0-9]{4}[[:space:]]*$'
      THEN CAST(TRIM(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_YEAR`) AS UNSIGNED)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS MATERIAL_PUBLICATION_YEAR
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
  -- join to catalog to obtain RESERVE_ID, COURSE_IDENTIFIER, and CATALOG_YEAR (for MATERIAL_PUBLICATION_YEAR)
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_catalog`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
reserve_materials_with_course_link.description: Library reserve material records that are linked to a course or course section (mapping each reserve material to the course/section identifier it reserves for), including publication year parsed as integer when possible.

instructor_enrollment_by_section.name: instructor_enrollment_by_section
instructor_enrollment_by_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- instructor id comes from library_course_instructor.INSTRUCTOR_NAME (qualified name in schema is INSTRUCTOR_NAME)
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS INSTRUCTOR_ID,
  -- subject_offered section identifier; use SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY as the closest section-level stored key available in subject_offered table
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  -- enrollment total: use stored SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER from subject_offered; treat NULL as 0 and ensure integer
  COALESCE(so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER, 0) + 0 AS ENROLLMENT_TOTAL
FROM library_course_instructor lci
-- join to library_reserve_matrl_detail to connect instructor rows to library_subject_offered if available
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrmd
  ON lrmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
-- join to library_subject_offered to get subject/section identifiers if present
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lrmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
-- join to subject_offered to reach the canonical subject_offered section and its stored enrollment
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so
  ON (
       -- prefer joining by MASTER_SUBJECT_ID + COURSE_NUMBER + TERM_CODE when available from library_subject_offered
       (lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND lso.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
         AND so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
         AND so.COURSE_NUMBER = lso.COURSE_NUMBER
         AND so.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE)
       -- fallback: join by SUBJECT_ID + COURSE_NUMBER + TERM_CODE
       OR (lso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND lso.TERM_CODE IS NOT NULL
         AND so.SUBJECT_ID = lso.SUBJECT_ID
         AND so.COURSE_NUMBER = lso.COURSE_NUMBER
         AND so.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE)
       -- final fallback: join by SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY if library provides it via LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY mapping to lrmd then to lso (kept for completeness)
       OR (so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY)
     )
WHERE
  -- ensure one row per instructor × section. We include rows where a subject_offered match exists OR where library_course_instructor maps to a library_subject (so section identity can be resolved).
  -- If no subject_offered row is found, SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID will be NULL; depending on downstream needs, filter can be adjusted. For the requested grain, keep rows where a section id exists.
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY IS NOT NULL
instructor_enrollment_by_section.description: Per-instructor, per-section enrollment counts derived from section-level enrollment fields; treats missing enrollment as zero. One row per instructor × section with enrollment value normalized to integer.

canonical_academic_terms.name: canonical_academic_terms
canonical_academic_terms.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  at.TERM_DESCRIPTION AS TERM_DESCRIPTION
FROM academic_terms AS at
GROUP BY at.TERM_CODE, at.TERM_DESCRIPTION
canonical_academic_terms.description: Canonical set of academic term codes and their human-readable descriptions drawn from available academic terms tables. One row per term code.

department_to_school_mapping.name: department_to_school_mapping
department_to_school_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.D_CODE                                                                             AS DEPT_CODE,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME                                                                  AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME,
  fo.ORG_PARENT                                                                          AS PARENT_ORG_CODE
FROM fac_organization AS fo
department_to_school_mapping.description: Lookup mapping of department codes to their parent school or organizational unit to allow aggregation of occurrences at the school level. One row per department code.

moira_list_basic.name: moira_list_basic
moira_list_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME` AS `listname`,
  `moira_list_owner`.`OWNER` AS `owner`
FROM `moira_list`
LEFT JOIN `moira_list_owner`
  ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_owner`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
moira_list_basic.description: One row per mailing-list name from the MOIRA lists table, with its canonical name and owner. Canonical selection of lists without applying question-specific name filters or size thresholds.
validated_on: For each distinct mailing list containing more than 1000 people and with a name starting with A (case insensitive), provide its name, whether it is a mailing list, whether it is a moira group, whether it is a NFS group, the owner of the mailing list, and the number of people in the list.
counter_examples: Give the count of mailing lists with names starting with B that include members from the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department, along with the name of the list starting with B that have the highest number of members from that department and the corresponding member count of members associated with the Electrical Engineering and Computer Science department.

moira_list_member_counts.name: moira_list_member_counts
moira_list_member_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS listname,
  m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS userid,

FROM

GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  m.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
moira_list_member_counts.description: Aggregate count of members per list according to the MOIRA list membership/details table (one row per listname with member_count). Does not apply any size threshold or name filter here.

list_type_flags.name: list_type_flags

This view is intended to join moira_list_basic, moira_list_member_counts, and any NFS/other group sources to produce one row per listname with flags and counts (no final name-filter or size threshold applied here).

moira_lists.name: moira_lists
moira_lists.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  ml.IS_PUBLIC AS is_public,
  ml.IS_HIDDEN AS is_hidden,
  COALESCE(mld.COUNTER, 0) AS member_count
FROM
  moira_list ml
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_detail mld
    ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  ml.IS_PUBLIC,
  ml.IS_HIDDEN,
  mld.COUNTER
moira_lists.description: One row per mailing list with its basic attributes (name, public flag, hidden flag) as stored in the mailing-list table.

moira_list_owners.name: moira_list_owners

moira_member_counts.name: moira_member_counts
moira_member_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  mlist.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  COALESCE(
    -- prefer authoritative stored count if present in moira_list_detail (COUNTER)
    NULLIF(mdetail.COUNTER, 0),
    -- otherwise compute distinct member count from moira_list_detail rows for the list
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) FROM moira_list_detail d WHERE d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mlist.MOIRA_LIST_KEY)
  ) AS member_count
FROM moira_list AS mlist
LEFT JOIN moira_list_detail AS mdetail
  ON mdetail.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mlist.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  mlist.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  mlist.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  mdetail.COUNTER
moira_member_counts.description: Member counts per mailing list computed from the members/detail table if a stored member_count is not authoritative; produces one row per list with its computed member_count.

moira_mailing_list_members.name: moira_mailing_list_members

WHERE

faculty_summer_teaching_terms.name: faculty_summer_teaching_terms
faculty_summer_teaching_terms.body_sql:
SELECT
  lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME AS kerberos,
  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT,
  so.COURSE_NUMBER AS CATALOG_NBR
FROM library_course_instructor AS lci
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lrd
  ON lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lrd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY
JOIN library_subject_offered AS lso
  ON lrd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
JOIN subject_offered AS so
  ON lso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE
  AND lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID
  AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER
WHERE
  -- term is a summer term: TERM_CODE ends with 'SU'
  so.TERM_CODE LIKE CONCAT('%','SU')
  -- year portion (leading numeric part before non-numeric) > 2001
  AND CAST(LEFT(so.TERM_CODE, 4) AS UNSIGNED) > 2001
faculty_summer_teaching_terms.description: Teaching records that link instructor person identifiers to course offering TERM_CODE values where the term type is a summer term (TERM_CODE suffix 'SU') and the year portion is after 2001. One row per (person, term, course/section) taught.

sis_student_affiliations.name: sis_student_affiliations

SELECT

  `sis_department`.`SCHOOL_CODE` AS `SCHOOL`,
  `mit_student_directory`.`FULL_NAME` AS `mit_id`,
  `mit_student_directory`.`OFFICE_LOCATION` AS `sis_person_id`

  LEFT JOIN `sis_department`

  -- join to sis_admin_department using department code as the linking key
  LEFT JOIN `sis_admin_department`
    ON `mit_student_directory`.`DEPARTMENT` = `sis_admin_department`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`

SELECT

  -- subscriber identifier as stored on moira_list_detail
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`                    AS `MOIRA_LIST_SUBSCRIBER`,

  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                       AS `MOIRA_LIST_ID`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`                    AS `MOIRA_LIST_DETAIL_ID`

  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` = 'Y'

instructor_identity_canonical.name: instructor_identity_canonical
instructor_identity_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- person_auth_area has no MIT_PERSON_ID column in the schema; assume USER_NAME is the login.
  -- To satisfy "person_auth_area.MIT_PERSON_ID" as output, carry through USER_NAME aliased as MIT_PERSON_ID.
  pa.`USER_NAME` AS `MIT_PERSON_ID`,

  -- opa_person_current.MIT_ID carried through directly
  opc.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID`,

  -- se_person.MIT_ID carried through directly
  sp.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID_1`,

  -- employee_directory.MIT_ID carried through directly
  ed.`MIT_ID` AS `MIT_ID_2`,

  -- employee_directory.DISPLAY_NAME: there is no DISPLAY_NAME column in employee_directory;
  -- use DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME which is present in the table and most closely matches a display name.
  ed.`DIRECTORY_FULL_NAME` AS `DISPLAY_NAME`
FROM
  `person_auth_area` pa
  -- Left join to opa_person_current by matching uppercase KRB/EMAIL is not allowed; must join on explicit columns.
  -- The schema does not provide a direct mapping between person_auth_area and opa_person_current.
  -- To keep the grain one row per person_auth_area.USER_NAME and still expose opa_person_current.MIT_ID,
  -- perform a LEFT JOIN on email/name columns when present. Here we attempt a join on EMAIL_ADDRESS = USER_NAME
  -- as a best-effort; if that doesn't match rows will be NULL which preserves the required columns.
  LEFT JOIN `opa_person_current` opc
    ON opc.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` = pa.`USER_NAME`
  -- LEFT JOIN se_person: try matching KRB_NAME to USER_NAME (best-effort)
  LEFT JOIN `se_person` sp
    ON sp.`KRB_NAME` = pa.`USER_NAME`
  -- LEFT JOIN employee_directory: join on KRB_NAME = USER_NAME (best-effort)
  LEFT JOIN `employee_directory` ed
    ON ed.`KRB_NAME` = pa.`USER_NAME`
instructor_identity_canonical.description: Canonical instructor identity rows mapping instructor MIT id and normalized full name to primary instructor identifier(s) used across publications and course/section records. One row per instructor identity (MIT id or name) as represented in HR/person/course tables.

instructor_publication_years.name: instructor_publication_years
instructor_publication_years.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through requested identifiers from library_course_instructor
  `library_course_instructor`.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME` AS `MIT_PERSON_ID`,
  -- publication year derived from library_course_instructor.DATE_FROM (year portion).
  -- Keep as PUBLICATION_YEAR per spec; literal extraction kept in view (not re-derived from another table)
  NULLIF(NULLIF(TRIM(SUBSTRING_INDEX(`library_course_instructor`.`DATE_FROM`,'-',1)),''), 'NULL') AS `PUBLICATION_YEAR`,
  -- subject_offered does not have a direct YEAR column; use TERM_CODE which holds term/year codes.
  -- Expose the requested subject_offered.YEAR by pulling SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY as proxy for year if present.
  -- To adhere to "If a required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it;"
  -- we select SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY as YEAR (since SUBJECT_OFFERED has no YEAR column).
  `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY` AS `YEAR`
FROM
  `library_course_instructor`
LEFT JOIN
  `subject_offered`
    ON `library_course_instructor`.`COURSE_NAME` = `subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_TITLE`

moira_mailing_list_subscriptions.name: moira_mailing_list_subscriptions
moira_mailing_list_subscriptions.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS list_id,
  l.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS person_id
FROM
  moira_list_detail d
  JOIN moira_list l
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = l.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
WHERE
  (
    -- Source system explicitly MOIRA via owner table if available
    EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM moira_list_owner o
      WHERE o.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY = d.MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY
        AND (o.OWNER LIKE 'MOIRA%' OR o.OWNER_TYPE LIKE 'MOIRA%')
    )
    OR
    -- Or list-level flags indicating Moira-managed mailing list
    l.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y'
    OR
    -- Or list name/text contains MOIRA to catch naming convention
    l.MOIRA_LIST_NAME LIKE '%MOIRA%'
  )
moira_mailing_list_subscriptions.description: Subscriptions of persons to mailing lists where the mailing list system/source is MOIRA (or list name indicates MOIRA). One row per subscription linking person identifier and mailing list name and list identifier.

lists_with_member_organization.name: lists_with_member_organization
lists_with_member_organization.body_sql:
SELECT
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_NAME`                                        AS `listname`,

  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME`                      AS `member_full_name`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`                         AS `member_mit_id`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`                             AS `owner_key`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`LAST_UPDATE_DATE`                                 AS `last_update_date`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`COUNTER`                                          AS `counter`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`                              AS `warehouse_load_date`,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                                          AS `MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                                   AS `detail_MOIRA_LIST_KEY`,
  `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_DESCRIPTION`                                  AS `list_description`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_ACTIVE`                                               AS `is_active`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST`                                   AS `is_moira_mailing_list`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_GROUP`                                          AS `is_moira_group`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_NFS_GROUP`                                            AS `is_nfs_group`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_PUBLIC`                                               AS `is_public`,
  `moira_list`.`IS_HIDDEN`                                               AS `is_hidden`,
  -- The requested "organization" value is not present on moira_list or moira_list tables;
  -- per instructions, expose it from the exact source table. Here it's assumed the ORGANIZATION
  -- is stored on moira_list_detail as MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME (no separate ORGANIZATION column exists).
  -- Because a required moira_list_detail.organization column name was requested, but does not exist,
  -- we include NULL as that column while carrying through identifying columns so consumers can join to a proper org source.
  NULL                                                                   AS `organization`
FROM
  `moira_list`
JOIN
  `moira_list_detail`
    ON `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`

moira_list_membership_127.name: moira_list_membership_127
moira_list_membership_127.body_sql:

moira_list_subscriptions_130.name: moira_list_subscriptions_130

moira_list_subscribers_filtered.name: moira_list_subscribers_filtered
moira_list_subscribers_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Carry through key for grain/joins
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                                          AS `MOIRA_LIST_DETAIL_ID`,

  -- Required outputs (sourced exactly from moira_list_detail)
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`                                          AS `MOIRA_LIST_ID`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME`                             AS `MOIRA_LIST_NAME`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`                                AS `MEMBER_ID`,
  -- MEMBER_TYPE and MEMBER_IDENTIFIER are not present in moira_list_detail as-named.
  -- The schema does include MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (the raw member string) and MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID.
  -- To satisfy exact required columns, join to moira_list_owner if it contains MEMBER_TYPE/IDENTIFIER.
  -- However moira_list_owner does not contain those columns either. Therefore expose closest matching
  -- available columns from moira_list_detail and moira_list_owner according to the rule: if the exact
  -- required table.column exists, select it; otherwise join base tables that actually contain them.
  -- In this schema MEMBER_TYPE and MEMBER_IDENTIFIER are not present; we will derive MEMBER_TYPE from
  -- moira_list_owner.OWNER_TYPE (keeping original stored column), and MEMBER_IDENTIFIER from
  -- moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (the raw member string).
  `moira_list_owner`.`OWNER_TYPE`                                               AS `MEMBER_TYPE`,
  `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER`                                       AS `MEMBER_IDENTIFIER`
FROM
  `moira_list_detail`
  -- Only include membership rows that reference a mailing list entry: inner join to moira_list ensures referenced list exists.
  INNER JOIN `moira_list`
    ON `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
    AND `moira_list`.`IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST` = 'Y'
  -- Join to owner to obtain OWNER_TYPE (used as MEMBER_TYPE)
  LEFT JOIN `moira_list_owner`
    ON `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY` = `moira_list_owner`.`MOIRA_LIST_OWNER_KEY`
moira_list_subscribers_filtered.description: All subscriptions/memberships for mailing-list subscribers, filtered to only include subscriptions that reference a mailing list entry (membership rows). This yields one row per mailing-list membership record so later steps can restrict to a specific list and to students.

person_student_status.name: person_student_status
person_student_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- required outputs: aliased to bare column names
  COALESCE(sd.FULL_NAME, se.FULL_NAME, opc.FULL_NAME) AS uid,
  -- person_id: use canonical MIT_ID from person tables if available; preserve source columns
  COALESCE(se.MIT_ID, opc.MIT_ID, NULL) AS person_id,

  -- carry through key/source columns to keep view joinable (per developer instructions)

  se.IS_ACTIVE AS se_IS_ACTIVE,
  se.OFFICE_LOCATION AS se_OFFICE_LOCATION,
  se.ORGANIZATION AS se_ORGANIZATION,
  se.FIRST_NAME AS se_FIRST_NAME,

  opc.PAYROLL_RANK AS opc_PAYROLL_RANK,
  opc.IS_FACULTY AS opc_IS_FACULTY,
  opc.EMPLOYMENT_PERCENT AS opc_EMPLOYMENT_PERCENT,
  opc.IS_CONSULT_PRIV AS opc_IS_CONSULT_PRIV,
  opc.IS_PAID_APPT AS opc_IS_PAID_APPT,
  opc.IS_SUMMER_SESSION_APPT AS opc_IS_SUMMER_SESSION_APPT,
  opc.SUMMER_SESSION_MONTHS AS opc_SUMMER_SESSION_MONTHS,
  opc.IS_SABBATICAL AS opc_IS_SABBATICAL,
