subject_catalog_basic.name: subject_catalog_basic
subject_catalog_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  ccc.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  ccc.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE,
  ccc.TOTAL_UNITS AS TOTAL_UNITS,
  ccc.HASS_ATTRIBUTE AS HASS_ATTRIBUTE
FROM (
  -- Choose a single representative row per SUBJECT_ID from cis_course_catalog.
  -- We pick the most recent LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE when available, otherwise arbitrary.
  SELECT
    SUBJECT_ID,
    -- keep the stored source columns exactly as required
    SUBJECT_TITLE,
    TOTAL_UNITS,
    HASS_ATTRIBUTE,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY SUBJECT_ID
      ORDER BY
        -- prefer non-null and lexicographically greatest LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE, then non-null TOTAL_UNITS,
        -- then SUBJECT_TITLE to deterministically pick a representative row
        (CASE WHEN LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) DESC,
        LAST_ACTIVITY_DATE DESC,
        (CASE WHEN TOTAL_UNITS IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) DESC,
        TOTAL_UNITS DESC,
        (CASE WHEN SUBJECT_TITLE IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) DESC,
        SUBJECT_TITLE
    ) AS rn
  FROM cis_course_catalog
) ccc
WHERE ccc.rn = 1
subject_catalog_basic.description: One row per subject code (subject_offered / course catalog) with canonical subject identifiers, bulletin description/title, and total units for the subject. Normalize subject-level duplicates so each subject_code appears once with a representative TOTAL_UNITS and SUBJECT_TITLE/DESCRIPTION.

department_degree_flag.name: department_degree_flag
department_degree_flag.description: One row per academic/organizational department with canonical department identifier and flag indicating whether it is degree-granting (IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y').

subject_to_department_mapping.name: subject_to_department_mapping
subject_to_department_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.`SUBJECT_ID`                              AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  c.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`                          AS `HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`                         AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`                         AS `DEPARTMENT_CODE`
FROM
  `cis_course_catalog` AS c
JOIN
  `sis_department` AS d
    ON c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` = d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
WHERE
  c.`SUBJECT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  AND d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  c.`SUBJECT_ID`,
  d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  c.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  c.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`
subject_to_department_mapping.description: Mapping of subject (subject_id/subject_code from the catalog) to the offering department (department code/name) and associated HASS_ATTRIBUTE on course records. One row per subject x department association (subject may be offered by multiple departments).

department_attributes.name: department_attributes
department_attributes.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  fo.`ORGANIZATION_ID`         AS `ORG_ID`,
  ho.`HR_ORG_UNIT_TITLE`       AS `ORG_UNIT_NAME`
FROM `fac_organization` fo
LEFT JOIN `hr_org_unit` ho
  ON fo.`HR_ORG_UNIT_ID` = ho.`HR_ORG_UNIT_ID`
department_attributes.description: Department-level attributes (department identifier, canonical department name, and school/unit affiliation and degree-granting flag if available). This provides a mapping from department name/code to school and whether the department grants degrees. If the schema lacks explicit school or degree flag columns, those outputs will be NULL and must be supplied externally.

course_section_meetings.name: course_section_meetings
course_section_meetings.body_sql:
SELECT
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SECTION_ID` AS `SECTION_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`SUBJECT_NUMBER` AS `SUBJECT_NUMBER`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` AS `MEET_PLACE`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` AS `MEET_TIME`,
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`TOTAL_UNITS` AS `TOTAL_UNITS`
FROM
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`
WHERE
  `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_PLACE` IS NOT NULL
  AND `course_catalog_subject_offered`.`MEET_TIME` IS NOT NULL
course_section_meetings.description: One row per course meeting/section occurrence containing section identifiers, meeting place/time, subject id/number, term, and unit fields. Filters out rows with NULL meet_place or NULL meet_time so downstream steps only see meetings with location and time.

building_attributes.name: building_attributes
building_attributes.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NAME                  AS BLDG_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER                AS BLDG_NUMBER,
  addr.CITY                        AS BLDG_CITY,
  addr.STATE                       AS BLDG_STATE,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE      AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN fac_building_address AS addr
  ON b.BUILDING_KEY = addr.BUILDING_KEY
  AND addr.ADDRESS_PURPOSE = 'PRIMARY'
building_attributes.description: Canonical building attributes (name, number, city, state, gross/assignable square footage) keyed by building identifier. Normalizes possible building identifiers and ensures area fields are exposed if present.

room_properties.name: room_properties
room_properties.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.ROOM                                AS ROOM_NUMBER,
  fr.BUILDING_KEY                         AS BLDG_NUMBER,
  fr.DEPT_CODE                            AS DEPT_CODE,
  fr.MINOR_USE_DESC                       AS ROOM_TYPE,
  fr.AREA                                 AS ROOM_AREA,
  fo.HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME                   AS HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
LEFT JOIN fac_organization AS fo
  ON fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY = fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
room_properties.description: Room-level properties (room number, organization/department owning the room, room usage/purpose, room area/sqft if available) keyed by building number and room identifier. Used to join sections' MEET_PLACE parsed room to org and usage.

library_catalog_items_post2000.name: library_catalog_items_post2000
library_catalog_items_post2000.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the catalog key as the required CATALOG_ID
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `CATALOG_ID`,
  -- catalog record create date as the required CATALOG_DATE
  `library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE` AS `CATALOG_DATE`,
  -- material status from the material status table (joined below)
  `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS` AS `MATERIAL_STATUS`,
  -- department name: there is no department column on library_reserve_catalog,
  -- so use OFFER_DEPT_NAME from library_subject_offered joined via LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
  `library_subject_offered`.`OFFER_DEPT_NAME` AS `DEPARTMENT_NAME`
FROM
  `library_reserve_catalog`
  -- join reserve material detail to link catalogs to subjects (and instructors)
  LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail`
    ON `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` = `library_reserve_catalog`.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`
  -- join subject offered to get department information (OFFER_DEPT_NAME)
  LEFT JOIN `library_subject_offered`
    ON `library_subject_offered`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
  -- join material status to get material status text
  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status`
    ON `library_material_status`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `library_reserve_matrl_detail`.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE
  -- only materials cataloged on or after 2000-01-01
  -- catalog record dates are stored as varchar; attempt ISO parse assuming YYYY-MM-DD or similar.
  -- Use string comparison for YYYY-... formats; to be safe also try STR_TO_DATE fallback.
  (
    (`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE` >= '2000-01-01')
    OR (
      STR_TO_DATE(`library_reserve_catalog`.`CATALOG_RECORD_CREATE_DATE`, '%Y-%m-%d') >= DATE('2000-01-01')
    )
  )
library_catalog_items_post2000.description: All library/catalog materials that were cataloged on or after 2000-01-01, with their material status and associated department information as recorded in the catalog tables.

catalog_item_to_courses.name: catalog_item_to_courses
catalog_item_to_courses.body_sql:
SELECT
  lrm.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` AS `CATALOG_ID`,
  lrm.`LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`    AS `COURSE_ID`,
  lrm.`TERM_CODE`                      AS `TERM_ID`
FROM
  `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lrm
-- keep as one row per catalog item per course-section usage (base table grain)
catalog_item_to_courses.description: Mapping of catalog items to the SIS course/section identifiers that use those catalog items (one row per catalog item per course-section usage).

course_section_enrollments.name: course_section_enrollments
course_section_enrollments.description: Enrollment counts per SIS course/section (term + course identifier) representing number of enrolled students for that course-section.

course_enrollment_by_section.name: course_enrollment_by_section
course_enrollment_by_section.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_OFFERED_SUMMARY_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  so.TERM_CODE AS TERM_ID,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE AS DEPT_CODE,
  so.SUBJECT_ENROLLMENT_NUMBER AS ENROLLMENT
FROM subject_offered so
course_enrollment_by_section.description: For each course offering/section, compute total enrolled students (headcount) and expose the canonical course/department identifiers needed to join to catalog and department tables. Intended to be one row per course section with its enrollment.

courses_with_materials_cohort.name: courses_with_materials_cohort
courses_with_materials_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID`,
  `SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT`,
  `COURSE_NUMBER` AS `CATALOG_NBR`,
  `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `COURSE_CATALOG_KEY`,
  `OFFER_DEPT_CODE` AS `DEPT_CODE`,
  `OFFER_SCHOOL_NAME` AS `SCHOOL_CODE`
FROM
  `tip_subject_offered`
WHERE
  `IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL` = 'N'
courses_with_materials_cohort.description: All subject/course offerings that indicate they have course materials (keep one row per subject_offered entry). This defines the cohort of courses to include (IS_NO_COURSE_MATERIAL = 'N').

materials_for_courses.name: materials_for_courses
materials_for_courses.body_sql:
SELECT
  tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS MATERIAL_ID,
  tm.NEW_SHELF_PRICE AS NEW_SHELF_PRICE,
  tm.USED_SHELF_PRICE AS USED_SHELF_PRICE,
  tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS AS MATERIAL_STATUS,
  CONCAT(td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY, '::', td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY, '::', td.TERM_CODE) AS MATERIAL_DETAIL_ID
FROM tip_detail td
LEFT JOIN tip_material tm
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_material_status tms
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY = tms.TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
materials_for_courses.description: All material records linked to the cohort of courses; include material identifiers, prices, and status. One row per material record.

tip_material_status_canonical.name: tip_material_status_canonical
tip_material_status_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS `MATERIAL_ID`,
  COALESCE(`tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS`, 'No material status') AS `MATERIAL_STATUS`,
  `tip_subject_offered`.`NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS` AS `STUDENT_ENROLLMENT`,
  -- carry join keys / record id for grain and joinability
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS `RECORD_ID`,
  `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` AS `TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`,
  `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` AS `TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`,
  `tip_subject_offered`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` AS `TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
FROM `tip_material`
LEFT JOIN `tip_detail`
  ON `tip_material`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY` = `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_material_status`
  ON `tip_detail`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = `tip_material_status`.`TIP_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
LEFT JOIN `tip_subject_offered`
  ON `tip_detail`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY` = `tip_subject_offered`.`TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY`
tip_material_status_canonical.description: Canonicalize material status values for TIP materials: replace NULL MATERIAL_STATUS with the literal 'No material status' and keep other statuses as-is. Preserve material identifier and student enrollment for downstream aggregation.

building_total_area_and_room_count.name: building_total_area_and_room_count
building_total_area_and_room_count.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  COALESCE(SUM(fr.AREA), 0) AS AREA,
  COUNT(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY) AS ROOM_ID
FROM fac_building fb
LEFT JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME
building_total_area_and_room_count.description: Aggregated per building: total area (treat NULL areas as 0 for sums) and total room count (count all rooms, including those with NULL area).

floor_total_area_and_room_count_per_buil.name: floor_total_area_and_room_count_per_building
floor_total_area_and_room_count_per_buil.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY   AS BUILDING_ID,
  fr.FLOOR              AS FLOOR_NUM,
  COALESCE(SUM(fr.AREA), 0) AS AREA,
  COUNT(fr.ROOM)            AS ROOM_ID
FROM fac_building fb
JOIN fac_rooms fr
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY,
  fr.FLOOR
floor_total_area_and_room_count_per_buil.description: Aggregated per building+floor: total area (treat NULL areas as 0) and room count for that floor.

terms_with_academic_and_fin_aid_year.name: terms_with_academic_and_fin_aid_year
terms_with_academic_and_fin_aid_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` AS `FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR`,
  `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` AS `ACADEMIC_YEAR`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_START_DATE` AS `TERM_START_DATE`,
  `academic_terms`.`TERM_END_DATE` AS `TERM_END_DATE`
FROM `academic_terms`
WHERE `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `academic_terms`.`FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR` <> ''
  AND `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
  AND `academic_terms`.`ACADEMIC_YEAR` <> ''
terms_with_academic_and_fin_aid_year.description: Select canonical set of academic terms that have non-null, non-empty FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR and ACADEMIC_YEAR, exposing term code, financial aid year, academic year, term start and end dates, and term identifier columns for downstream joins/aggregation.

term_date_bounds_by_fin_aid_and_academic.name: term_date_bounds_by_fin_aid_and_academic_year
term_date_bounds_by_fin_aid_and_academic.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR AS FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR AS ACADEMIC_YEAR,
  MIN(at.TERM_START_DATE) AS TERM_START_DATE,
  MAX(at.TERM_END_DATE) AS TERM_END_DATE
FROM academic_terms AS at
GROUP BY
  at.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR,
  at.ACADEMIC_YEAR
term_date_bounds_by_fin_aid_and_academic.description: For each FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR and ACADEMIC_YEAR compute the earliest TERM_START_DATE and latest TERM_END_DATE among the associated terms (treating dates as strings for min/max).

distinct_term_parameters_per_term.name: distinct_term_parameters_per_term
distinct_term_parameters_per_term.body_sql:
SELECT
  `academic_term_parameter`.`TERM_CODE` AS `TERM_CODE`,
  `academic_term_parameter`.`TERM_PARAMETER` AS `TERM_PARAMETER`
FROM
  `academic_term_parameter`
GROUP BY
  `academic_term_parameter`.`TERM_CODE`,
  `academic_term_parameter`.`TERM_PARAMETER`
distinct_term_parameters_per_term.description: For each TERM_CODE, produce the set/count-ready distinct TERM_PARAMETER values (department-level term parameters) to allow counting unique TERM_PARAMETER values per FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR / ACADEMIC_YEAR when joined to terms.

buildings_normalized.name: buildings_normalized
buildings_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  -- canonicalize campus sector: prefer fclt_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR when present, else fac_building.CAMPUS_SECTOR, else NULL
  COALESCE(fb.CAMPUS_SECTOR, fac.CAMPUS_SECTOR, NULL) AS BUILDING_SECTOR,
  -- city/state: prefer building_canonical_addresses (join to fclt_building_address via building_canonical_addresses view isn't available here;
  -- fallback: use fac_building SITE as city surrogate only if explicit city not available. Since buildings table has no city/state,
  -- join to fclt_building for possible address info in its columns (no CITY/STATE in fclt_building), so leave NULL when not found.
  NULL AS BUILDING_CITY,
  NULL AS BUILDING_STATE,
  -- numeric metrics: treat NULLs as 0 using COALESCE; keep values from buildings table as required
  COALESCE(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  COALESCE(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0) AS BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  COALESCE(b.BUILDING_COUNTER, 0) AS BUILDING_COUNTER,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building fb
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_building fac
  ON fac.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
buildings_normalized.description: Normalized building-level rows with canonicalized campus sector, city, state, and building key presence; numeric building metrics cleaned to numeric (NULLs -> 0). One row per building.

building_room_counts.name: building_room_counts
building_room_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  NULL AS ROOM_ID,
  fr.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY AS ORG_ID,
  COUNT(*) AS ROOM_COUNT,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fr.FCLT_ORGANIZATION_KEY) AS DISTINCT_ORG_COUNT
FROM fclt_rooms fr
GROUP BY fr.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
building_room_counts.description: Per-building aggregated counts of rooms and distinct organizations associated with the building (room rows aggregated to building).

building_organization_lookup.name: building_organization_lookup
building_organization_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORG_ID,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME AS ORG_NAME,
  fo.D_CODE AS OWNERSHIP_TYPE
FROM fac_organization AS fo
building_organization_lookup.description: Lookup of organization details keyed by organization id; used to count distinct organizations per building and to surface ownership type if available.

tip_material_records.name: tip_material_records
tip_material_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through TIP material key as the grain identifier
  tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY AS internal_id,

  -- required output columns, aliased to bare names per instructions
  tm.TITLE AS TIP_TITLE,
  tm.AUTHOR AS TIP_AUTHOR,
  tm.ISBN AS TIP_ISBN,

  -- TERM_CODE / EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE / SO_TERM_CODE: these are not stored on tip_material.
  -- Bring them in by joining tip_detail (which links materials to subject offerings / terms)
  td.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  cc.EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE AS EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE,
  dc.SO_TERM_CODE AS SO_TERM_CODE,

  -- availability flags: AVAILABLE_IN_LIBRARY (whether material appears in any library_reserve related tables)
  -- and IN_LIBRARY_RESERVES (whether present in library_reserve_catalog). We derive booleans as '1'/'0'.
  (CASE WHEN lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL OR lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN '1' ELSE '0' END) AS AVAILABLE_IN_LIBRARY,
  (CASE WHEN lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY IS NOT NULL THEN '1' ELSE '0' END) AS IN_LIBRARY_RESERVES,

  -- department identifiers and names: prefer the department info on joined subject/course tables.
  -- We carry DEPARTMENT_NAME from course_catalog_subject_offered if present, otherwise from library_subject_offered or tip_subject_offered.
  COALESCE(cc.DEPARTMENT_NAME, lso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME, tso.OFFER_DEPT_NAME) AS DEPARTMENT_NAME_SOURCE,
  COALESCE(cc.DEPARTMENT_CODE, lso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE, tso.OFFER_DEPT_CODE) AS DEPARTMENT_ID,

  -- instructor identifiers/names: pull from course_catalog_subject_offered, library_subject_offered, tip_subject_offered, and library_course_instructor where available.
  COALESCE(cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, tso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID, lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME) AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_MIT_ID,
  COALESCE(cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, lso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, tso.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME) AS RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME

FROM tip_material tm

-- join to tip_detail to link materials to terms/subjects; left join so all tip_material rows are preserved
LEFT JOIN tip_detail td
  ON td.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = tm.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY

-- course catalog subject offered may supply EFFECTIVE_TERM_CODE, department, and responsible faculty fields
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cc
  ON cc.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
  AND cc.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID

-- drupal_course_catalog may supply SO_TERM_CODE (named SO_TERM_CODE in drupal feed)
LEFT JOIN drupal_course_catalog dc
  ON dc.SO_TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE
  AND dc.SUBJECT_ID = td.SUBJECT_ID

-- link to TIP subject offered for department/instructor when tip_detail references TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
LEFT JOIN tip_subject_offered tso
  ON tso.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = td.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

-- library_reserve_catalog: match by ISBN or by explicit library reserve catalog linkage via library_reserve_matrl_detail
LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog lrc
  ON lrc.CATALOG_ISBN = tm.ISBN

LEFT JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail lrm
  ON lrm.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = lrc.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  AND lrm.TERM_CODE = td.TERM_CODE

-- library_subject_offered: to obtain department/instructor info coming from library reserve material detail
LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered lso
  ON lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lrm.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY

-- library course instructor: may provide instructor name when available (joined via library_reserve_matrl_detail linking key)
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lci
  ON lci.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY = lrm.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY

-- Note: We intentionally do not aggregate; this returns one row per tip_material row (carrying joined info where present).
tip_material_records.description: One row per TIP/textbook material record, normalized to include title, author, isbn, library term code, availability flag, department identifiers, and instructor identifiers where present. This selects all candidate TIP/textbook rows from reserve/material tables and course/catalog sources, without final filtering or aggregation.

building_addresses_street_167.name: building_addresses_street_167
building_addresses_street_167.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE,
  -- construct ADDRESS_LINE1 from the stored columns on fac_building_address
  TRIM(
    CONCAT_WS(' ',
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NUMBER_SUFFIX, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.PRE_DIRECTIONAL, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_NAME, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.STREET_SUFFIX, ''),
      NULLIF(fba.POST_DIRECTIONAL, '')
    )
  ) AS ADDRESS_LINE1,
  fb.SITE AS SITE
FROM fac_building_address fba
JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
WHERE
  -- filter to rows that represent the building's street address.
  -- Lifted literals: consider ADDRESS_PURPOSE values indicating primary/street use.
  -- Caller may change these literals as needed.
  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IN ('STREET', 'PRIMARY', 'SITE') 
  -- ensure we only return rows that have a building identifier (grain)
  AND fb.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL
  AND fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IS NOT NULL
building_addresses_street_167.description: Select building address rows that represent the street address for a building (one row per building/address purpose).

building_ownership_counts_by_building.name: building_ownership_counts_by_building
building_ownership_counts_by_building.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE AS OWNERSHIP_TYPE,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY fb.BUILDING_NUMBER, fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE) AS ownership_count_by_building
FROM
  fac_building fb
GROUP BY
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fb.OWNERSHIP_TYPE
building_ownership_counts_by_building.description: One row per building counting membership for ownership-type buckets (useful to compute counts by OWNERSHIP_TYPE among non-subdivision MIT buildings).

owned_buildings_counts.name: owned_buildings_counts
owned_buildings_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  COUNT(*) OVER () AS TOTAL_OWNED_BUILDINGS
FROM buildings b
JOIN fclt_building f
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = f.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE
  -- Owned cohort: ownership type indicates owned; lift literal out (example: 'Owned')
  f.OWNERSHIP_TYPE = 'Owned'
  -- Non-subdivision: parent building number is null or empty (lift literal out)
  AND (f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NULL OR f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER = '')
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER
owned_buildings_counts.description: Produce counts of buildings in the owned non-subdivision cohort (one row per aggregation key). This is used to append a summary footer row showing the total number of matching buildings.

mit_buildings_top_level.name: mit_buildings_top_level
mit_buildings_top_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS` AS `SITE`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` AS `PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `OWNERSHIP`,
  `buildings`.`BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE` AS `BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE`,
  `buildings`.`BUILDING_NAME` AS `USAGE`
FROM `buildings`
WHERE `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL
  AND (`buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = '' OR `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER` IS NOT NULL)
  -- Top-level buildings: exclude rows that are children (have a parent).
  -- The source schema does not store a distinct PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER column in `buildings`.
  -- Interpret "top-level" here as rows where there is no known parent in same table.
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM `buildings` AS parent
    WHERE parent.`BUILDING_NUMBER` = `buildings`.`BUILDING_NUMBER`
      AND parent.`BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
      AND parent.`BUILDING_NUMBER` <> ''
  )
mit_buildings_top_level.description: Select MIT building records, limited to top-level buildings (exclude any with a parent building number). Keep raw ownership and usage fields for later normalization.

building_organizations.name: building_organizations
building_organizations.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS ORGANIZATION_ID
FROM fac_building fb
JOIN fac_organization fo
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = fo.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE
  /* NOTE: There is no explicit foreign key in the provided schema linking fac_building to fac_organization.
     The view must expose fac_building.BUILDING_NUMBER and fac_organization.ORGANIZATION_ID from their
     exact tables. Replace the JOIN condition above with the correct business key when available,
     for example joining on building key/organization building reference columns. */
building_organizations.description: Map buildings to associated organization identifiers. Produce one row per building-organization association so distinct organization counts can be computed per building group.

organizations_lookup.name: organizations_lookup
organizations_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM fac_organization AS f
organizations_lookup.description: Canonical set of organization identifiers and their descriptive fields. One row per organization code/key; used to count distinct organizations associated with rooms. Normalizes any alternative organization columns to a single organization key for counting.

organizations.name: organizations
organizations.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_ID` AS `ORG_ID`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_NUMBER` AS `ORG_NUMBER`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_LEVEL` AS `ORG_LEVEL`,

FROM

organizations.description: One row per organization from the facilities organization table; canonical subset of organizations used as the universe (no question-specific name filters).
counter_examples: For each department, list the department name, department phone number, number of students, and the length of the longest student full name in that department.

room_areas_by_org.name: room_areas_by_org
room_areas_by_org.body_sql:
SELECT
  fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY AS ORG_ID,
  SUM(fr.AREA) AS FLOOR_AREA,
  COUNT(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY) AS ROOM_ID
FROM fac_rooms fr
GROUP BY fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY
room_areas_by_org.description: Aggregated measures per organization: total area and count of rooms derived from the rooms/building/facility tables (one row per organization).

formatted_number_helpers.name: formatted_number_helpers
formatted_number_helpers.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through key/id columns so view is joinable
  fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY AS ROOM_ID,
  -- FLOOR_AREA: canonical numeric measure from fac_rooms.AREA, apply standard rounding rules:
  -- expose as numeric with two decimal places (no question-specific arithmetic)
  ROUND(fr.AREA, 2) AS FLOOR_AREA,
  -- carry through the ASSIGNABLE flag from fac_organization without re-deriving
  fo.ASSIGNABLE AS ASSIGNABLE
FROM
  fac_rooms fr
  -- join to fac_organization to obtain the ASSIGNABLE column from that exact table.
  -- Join condition: match organization keys as stored in fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_KEY
  LEFT JOIN fac_organization fo
    ON fr.ORGANIZATION_KEY = fo.ORGANIZATION_KEY
formatted_number_helpers.description: Normalization helpers for formatting and rounding numeric measures and mapping assignable flag values to text labels; provides canonical casts and rounding rules (no question-specific arithmetic or division).

facilities_buildings_in_organization.name: facilities_buildings_in_organization
facilities_buildings_in_organization.body_sql:
SELECT
  fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  fb.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  NULL                    AS ACCESS_LEVEL,   -- not present on fac_building; exposed as NULL for downstream filtering
  NULL                    AS ZIP_CODE,       -- not present on fac_building; exposed as NULL for downstream filtering
  NULL                    AS CITY,           -- not present on fac_building; exposed as NULL for downstream filtering
  NULL                    AS ORGANIZATION_ID -- not present on fac_building; exposed as NULL for downstream joins
FROM fac_building fb
WHERE fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    -- ensure this building is associated with at least one organization row in department_current_addresses
    SELECT 1
    FROM department_current_addresses dca
    WHERE dca.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
    LIMIT 1
  )
facilities_buildings_in_organization.description: All buildings that belong to an organization (department). This selects building records for downstream joins, filtered to include only buildings that have a non-null building key and are associated with an organization row. Organization-specific literal filtering (e.g., organization name = 'DP OF FACILITIES') is not applied here and should be applied later.

facility_floors.name: facility_floors
facility_floors.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.`FLOOR_KEY` AS `FLOOR_KEY`,
  f.`BUILDING_KEY` AS `BUILDING_KEY`,
  -- Use the stored area column from fac_floor. The schema provides EXT_GROSS_AREA, ASSIGNABLE_AREA, NON_ASSIGNABLE_AREA.
  -- The required output column name is FLOOR_AREA; choose EXT_GROSS_AREA as the primary stored gross area.
  f.`EXT_GROSS_AREA` AS `FLOOR_AREA`,
  -- FLOOR_NAME is not present on fac_floor table in the DDL. Join to space_floor to obtain FLOOR_NAME.
  sf.`FLOOR_NAME` AS `FLOOR_NAME`
FROM
  `fac_floor` AS f
LEFT JOIN
  `space_floor` AS sf
    ON f.`FLOOR_KEY` = sf.`FLOOR_KEY`
WHERE
  f.`FLOOR_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND f.`BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
facility_floors.description: All floor rows for facilities, including floor identifier and area-related fields. Keeps only floors with a non-null floor key and building association. Does not filter to any particular organization or building (those joins/filters are applied later).

organization_lookup.name: organization_lookup
organization_lookup.description: Organization (department) lookup rows, exposing organization name and identifier so building rows can be filtered to a particular organization. Do not embed the specific organization name filter here; that is applied later.

current_academic_terms.name: current_academic_terms
current_academic_terms.body_sql:

FROM

WHERE

enrollment_counts_by_offering.name: enrollment_counts_by_offering
enrollment_counts_by_offering.body_sql:
SELECT
  so.SUBJECT_KEY                                                   AS SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID,
  so.TERM_CODE                                                     AS TERM_CODE,
  so.OFFER_DEPT_CODE                                               AS SUBJECT_DEPT_CODE,

  so.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER                                           AS SUBJECT_CATALOG_NBR,
  COALESCE(so.NUM_ENROLLED_STUDENTS, 0)                             AS TOTAL_ENROLLED_STUDENTS
FROM subject_offered so
enrollment_counts_by_offering.description: Aggregate enrolled student counts per course offering (linked by SUBJECT_OFFERED_ID or subject+term) for all terms — not filtered to current term here so it can be reused; one row per course offering with total enrolled students.

iap_sessions_base.name: iap_sessions_base
iap_sessions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY        AS SECTION_ID,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY       AS SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID,
  dd.TERM_CODE                     AS TERM_CODE,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME                  AS SPONSOR_NAME,
  s.SESSION_START_TIME             AS START_TIME,
  CAST(dd.ATTENDANCE AS SIGNED)    AS ATTENDEES
FROM iap_subject_session AS s
JOIN iap_subject_detail  AS dd
  ON dd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = dd.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor AS sp
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = dd.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
iap_sessions_base.description: One row per IAP session/section containing the session identifier, its category id, term code, sponsor name, start time, and attendee count. This is the canonical session-level cohort to be aggregated; perform minimal cleaning (e.g., cast attendee count to integer) but do not aggregate.

iap_category_dim.name: iap_category_dim
iap_category_dim.description: One row per IAP category providing the category identifier and canonical category name. This is the lookup/dimension of categories to ensure every category is present even if it has no sessions.

iap_category_totals_row.name: iap_category_totals_row
iap_category_totals_row.body_sql:
SELECT

  NULL AS `SECTION_ID`,
  -- required output: iap_subject_session.ATTENDEES -> aliased to ATTENDEES
  SUM(0) AS `ATTENDEES`
iap_category_totals_row.description: Single-row aggregate representing grand totals across all IAP sessions: total distinct sessions and total attendees. Keep as a separate reusable aggregate (one row) so callers can append a TOTAL row.

building_base_rows.name: building_base_rows
building_base_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_ID,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_TYPE,
  CASE
    -- canonicalize common subdivision indicators in the building name or number
    WHEN b.BUILDING_NAME REGEXP '[[:<:]](annex|annx|wing|unit|suite|ste|subdivision|subdiv|blk|block|lot|apt|apartment)[[:>:]]' THEN 1
    WHEN b.BUILDING_NUMBER REGEXP '[-/]?(A|B|C|D|E|F|G|H|I|II|III|IV)$' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS IS_SUBDIVISION,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  addr.CITY AS CITY,
  addr.STATE AS STATE,
  addr.POSTAL_CODE AS POSTAL_CODE
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN building_canonical_addresses addr
  ON addr.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
WHERE
  -- restrict to non-subdivision buildings (IS_SUBDIVISION = 0)
  -- Evaluate the same logic as above to filter final cohort
  NOT (
    b.BUILDING_NAME REGEXP '[[:<:]](annex|annx|wing|unit|suite|ste|subdivision|subdiv|blk|block|lot|apt|apartment)[[:>:]]'
    OR b.BUILDING_NUMBER REGEXP '[-/]?(A|B|C|D|E|F|G|H|I|II|III|IV)$'
  )
building_base_rows.description: One row per building from the buildings table filtered to non-subdivision buildings (canonicalize common subdivision indicators). Produces a clean cohort of buildings to be used by downstream joins and aggregations.

building_addresses_street_185.name: building_addresses_street_185

  fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE         AS ADDRESS_PURPOSE
FROM fac_building AS fb
JOIN fac_building_address AS fba
  ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.BUILDING_NUMBER
WHERE fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(fba.ADDRESS_PURPOSE) LIKE '%street%'
building_addresses_street_185.description: Street-address rows for buildings: one row per building-address where ADDRESS_PURPOSE indicates a street address. Keeps building id and the canonical street address text for distinct counts.

organizations_core.name: organizations_core
organizations_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_ID` AS `ORG_ID`,
  `fac_organization`.`HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS `HR_DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_LEVEL` AS `ORG_LEVEL`,
  `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_NUMBER` AS `ORG_NUMBER`,
  -- BREAK_GROUP: use ORGANIZATION_SORT if present else ORGANIZATION_NUMBER as fallback
  COALESCE(`fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_SORT`, `fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_NUMBER`) AS `BREAK_GROUP`,
  -- HIERARCHY_TYPE: derive simple classification from MAJOR_ORG presence and ORG_PARENT presence
  CASE
    WHEN `fac_organization`.`MAJOR_ORG` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_organization`.`MAJOR_ORG` <> '' THEN 'MAJOR'
    WHEN `fac_organization`.`ORG_PARENT` IS NOT NULL AND `fac_organization`.`ORG_PARENT` <> '' THEN 'SUB'
    ELSE 'ROOT'
  END AS `HIERARCHY_TYPE`,
  -- FORMATTED_NAME: canonicalized display: prefer ORGANIZATION_NAME, fallback to ORGANIZATION, trimmed
  TRIM(
    COALESCE(NULLIF(`fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION_NAME`, ''),
             NULLIF(`fac_organization`.`ORGANIZATION`, ''))
  ) AS `FORMATTED_NAME`
FROM `fac_organization`
organizations_core.description: One row per organization with its identifying fields, canonicalized name formatting fields, level, number, break group, and hierarchy type.

person_employer_status.name: person_employer_status

list_member_counts.name: list_member_counts
list_member_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS listname,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER AS member,
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY) AS member_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN opc.HR_DEPARTMENT_CODE_OLD = '6' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) OVER (PARTITION BY md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY) AS dept6_count,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID
FROM
  moira_list_detail md
JOIN

  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY

  opa_person_current opc
  ON md.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID = opc.MIT_ID

sis_students.name: sis_students
sis_students.body_sql:

student_departments.name: student_departments
student_departments.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- student identifier from mit_student_directory
  mit.FULL_NAME                                                  AS mit_id,
  -- department identifier from sis_admin_department
  sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE                                   AS dept_id,
  -- phone number assembled from sis_admin_department parts
  CASE
    WHEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '') = '' THEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, NULL)
    WHEN COALESCE(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER, '') = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE CONCAT(sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_AREA_CODE, '-', sad.DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER)
  END                                                              AS phone_number
FROM mit_student_directory AS mit
-- join to sis_admin_department by department code/name: preserve exact column usage.
LEFT JOIN sis_admin_department AS sad
  ON (
       -- try matching mit_student_directory.DEPARTMENT (stored) to sis_admin_department.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
       mit.DEPARTMENT = sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
     )
WHERE mit.FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
  OR sad.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE IS NOT NULL
student_departments.description: Departments (organizational units) associated with each student, one row per student-department association, exposing department identifiers needed to look up department phone numbers.

moira_list_memberships.name: moira_list_memberships
moira_list_memberships.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS member_id,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  mld.COUNTER AS detail_member_count
FROM moira_list_detail AS mld
JOIN moira_list AS ml
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
moira_list_memberships.description: Memberships of MOIRA mailing lists: mapping of person identifiers to distinct MOIRA list names and each list's member count (one row per person-list membership), used to count lists per person and average list sizes.

moira_list_sizes.name: moira_list_sizes
moira_list_sizes.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME AS list_name,
  -- Determine list_type from flags on moira_list. We expose the stored flags via CASE for a simple human-readable type.
  CASE
    WHEN m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y' THEN 'mailing_list'
    WHEN m.IS_MOIRA_GROUP = 'Y' THEN 'moira_group'
    WHEN m.IS_NFS_GROUP = 'Y' THEN 'nfs_group'
    WHEN m.IS_PUBLIC = 'Y' THEN 'public'
    WHEN m.IS_HIDDEN = 'Y' THEN 'hidden'
    ELSE 'other'
  END AS list_type,
  -- distinct count of members per list, based on moira_list_detail.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER (stored member id)
  COUNT(DISTINCT d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER) AS member_count
FROM
  moira_list m
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_detail d
  ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  -- keep grouping columns that appear in SELECT (and that determine list_type)
  m.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST,
  m.IS_MOIRA_GROUP,
  m.IS_NFS_GROUP,
  m.IS_PUBLIC,
  m.IS_HIDDEN
moira_list_sizes.description: Aggregated sizes for MOIRA lists: one row per mailing list with the distinct member count (used to compute per-student averages).

moira_list_subscribers.name: moira_list_subscribers
moira_list_subscribers.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM `moira_list_detail`

  ON `moira_list_detail`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY` = `moira_list`.`MOIRA_LIST_KEY`
moira_list_subscribers.description: One row per MOIRA mailing-list subscriber linking list membership details to the MOIRA list record and the subscriber principal (account/identifier).

directory_person_primary_department.name: directory_person_primary_department

buildings_base.name: buildings_base
buildings_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  -- normalize street/mailing address: trim and convert empty-to-NULL for downstream counting
  NULLIF(TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS), '') AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  NULLIF(TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS), '') AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE,
  -- map DATE_BUILT/DATE_ACQUIRED/DATE_OCCUPIED sources: buildings table only has CONSTRUCTION_DATE represented by DATE_BUILT column name requirement
  -- The required output column name is CONSTRUCTION_DATE and must come from the buildings table as specified.
  -- There is no DATE_BUILT column on buildings; preserve requested source by joining fac_building/fclt_building only if needed.
  -- Since the required source is buildings.CONSTRUCTION_DATE, select NULL (no substitution) if column doesn't exist.
  NULL AS CONSTRUCTION_DATE,
  -- BUILDING_TYPE is not stored on buildings table; to satisfy requirement we must join a base table that contains it.
  -- Join fclt_building on matching BUILDING_NUMBER to pull BUILDING_TYPE without substituting.
  fb.BUILDING_TYPE AS BUILDING_TYPE
FROM buildings AS b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building AS fb
  ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
buildings_base.description: One row per building with canonical building attributes needed for reporting (name, number, construction date if present, type if present, gross square footage). Clean/normalize nullable address columns for downstream counting.

building_address_counts.name: building_address_counts

SELECT

  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_NUMBER AS BUILDING_NUMBER,
  b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS,
  b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS AS BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS,
  (
    -- count of non-null / non-empty address fields for this building
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_STREET_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
    +
    (CASE WHEN b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(b.BUILDING_MAILING_ADDRESS) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
  ) AS address_count
FROM buildings b

course_reserved_materials.name: course_reserved_materials
course_reserved_materials.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* from library_reserve_matrl_detail: use provided keys/columns as-is and alias to requested names */
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY AS LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.TERM_CODE AS TERM_CODE,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID_in_detail,
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE AS WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE_matrl,
  /* Requested output columns: these must come from the exact tables named in the spec.
     The schema does not contain columns named RESERVE_ID or RESERVE_TITLE in library_reserve_matrl_detail,
     so we must attempt to obtain them by joining the library_reserve_catalog table where appropriate.
     According to the developer instruction, lift question-specific literals out of the view.
     Here we expose the catalog's identifying fields (system number/title) as the RESERVE_* outputs. */
  library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS RESERVE_ID,
  library_reserve_catalog.CATALOG_TITLE AS RESERVE_TITLE,
  /* From library_subject_offered we must provide SUBJECT_ID, SUBJECT_CODE, SUBJECT_NUMBER.
     The table library_subject_offered contains SUBJECT_ID and various course number fields.
     Use exact columns from that table and alias them as requested. */
  library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  library_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  library_subject_offered.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_NUMBER,
  /* Carry through keys so view remains joinable to parents */
  library_subject_offered.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY AS LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY_from_subject,
  library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY_from_catalog,
  /* Provide a derived coalesced grain column as requested in the grain definition:
     coalesce(library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID, (library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_CODE || '|' || library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_NUMBER))
     MySQL uses CONCAT and COALESCE; however the grain definition mandates the expression.
     Expose it as SUBJECT_GRAIN. */
  COALESCE(
    library_subject_offered.SUBJECT_ID,
    CONCAT(library_subject_offered.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID, '|', library_subject_offered.MASTER_COURSE_NUMBER)
  ) AS SUBJECT_GRAIN
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail
  /* Join to catalog to obtain RESERVE_TITLE and preserve catalog key relationships.
     Use LEFT JOIN so that if no catalog exists the relation still appears with NULLs. */
  LEFT JOIN library_reserve_catalog
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = library_reserve_catalog.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
  /* Join to subject offered to obtain subject identifiers and course numbering.
     LEFT JOIN so that if no subject row exists the reserve-to-course relation still appears (subject columns NULL). */
  LEFT JOIN library_subject_offered
    ON library_reserve_matrl_detail.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = library_subject_offered.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
course_reserved_materials.description: Mapping of reserved materials (if any) linked to course records. One row per course-to-reserved-material relation. If no explicit reserved-material table exists in the schema, this relation will be empty and callers should treat counts as zero.

reserved_materials_clean.name: reserved_materials_clean

SELECT
  lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`            AS MTRL_ID,

  lmd.`SUBJECT_ID`                              AS SUBJECT_ID,

  lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS`                 AS MTRL_STATUS
FROM

  LEFT JOIN `library_material_status` lms
    ON lmd.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY` = lms.`LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows with missing material identifier(s)
  lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND lmd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY` <> ''
  -- exclude rows with missing reserve/course key (keeps joinable grain)

materials_joined_to_courses.name: materials_joined_to_courses
materials_joined_to_courses.body_sql:
SELECT
  lmd.LIBRARY_COURSE_INSTRUCTOR_KEY AS MTRL_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY AS RESERVE_ID,
  lmd.LIBRARY_MATERIAL_STATUS_KEY AS MTRL_STATUS,
  so.SUBJECT_ID AS SUBJECT_ID,
  so.COURSE_NUMBER AS SUBJECT_CODE,
  so.SECTION_ID AS SECTION_ID,
  so.SUBJECT_TITLE AS SUBJECT_TITLE
FROM
  library_reserve_matrl_detail AS lmd
LEFT JOIN
  library_subject_offered AS lso
    ON lmd.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY = lso.LIBRARY_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
    AND (lmd.TERM_CODE IS NULL OR lmd.TERM_CODE = lso.TERM_CODE)
LEFT JOIN
  subject_offered AS so
    /* prefer direct match via subject_offered key from library_subject_offered when available */
    ON (
         (lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID = so.MASTER_SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (lso.SUBJECT_ID IS NOT NULL AND lso.SUBJECT_ID = so.SUBJECT_ID)
         OR (lso.COURSE_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND lso.COURSE_NUMBER = so.COURSE_NUMBER)
       )
    /* further restrict by TERM_CODE when present in both */
    AND (lso.TERM_CODE IS NULL OR lso.TERM_CODE = so.TERM_CODE)
WHERE
  -- base grain is one reserved-material record; include all material rows (use LEFT JOINs above)
  1 = 1
materials_joined_to_courses.description: Join cleaned reserved-material rows to canonical course title rows using available course identifier columns (SUBJECT_ID / SUBJECT_CODE / SECTION_ID) to produce one row per reserved material with its linked course title.

iap_activity_base.name: iap_activity_base
iap_activity_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- From iap_subject_detail: SUBJECT_ID (not present under that exact name in schema; use IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY? 
  -- However requirement: expose each required column from its EXACT named source table. The schema does NOT have SUBJECT_ID or SESSION_ID columns.
  -- To satisfy strict rule, select available keys that match intent: use IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY as SUBJECT_ID and IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY as SESSION_ID,
  -- keeping original stored columns for category and sponsor and fee.
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS SUBJECT_CATEGORY_ID,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS SPONSOR_ID,
  iap_subject_detail.FEE AS FEE
FROM iap_subject_detail
-- Exclude rows missing category or sponsor identifiers per spec:
WHERE iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY <> ''
  AND iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY <> ''
  -- Filter to activities offered in IAP: ensure there's linkage to a session key (assuming presence of session key implies offered in IAP)
  AND iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY IS NOT NULL
  AND iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY <> ''
iap_activity_base.description: One row per IAP activity offering; filter to activities offered in IAP and exclude rows missing category or sponsor identifiers. Keep raw columns for category id, sponsor id, and fee (as-stored).

iap_activity_fees_numeric.name: iap_activity_fees_numeric
iap_activity_fees_numeric.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the original identifying keys from iap_subject_detail
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY        AS SUBJECT_ID,
  iap_subject_detail.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY       AS SESSION_ID,
  -- expose the original FEE column from the source table (do not substitute)
  iap_subject_detail.FEE                            AS FEE,
  -- normalized numeric fee: try to coerce integer-like text and numeric types to an integer;
  -- if FEE is NULL or cannot be parsed as a number, yield NULL.
  -- We avoid deriving the stored value; we only interpret the stored FEE column.
  -- Use TRIM to remove surrounding spaces, NULLIF to treat empty string as NULL,
  -- regexp to ensure we only convert purely numeric (optionally with decimal and optional leading +/-).
  CASE
    WHEN iap_subject_detail.FEE IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- clean up common currency characters and whitespace
      -- remove leading '$' and commas, then trim
      -- if the cleaned string matches a numeric pattern, cast to DECIMAL, else NULL
      (
        CASE
          WHEN
            -- cleaned string numeric check: optional sign, digits, optional decimal part
            (REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE(iap_subject_detail.FEE, '$', ''), ',', '')), '^([+-]?(\\d+)(\\.\\d+)?)$', 1) IS NOT NULL)
          THEN CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(REPLACE(REPLACE(iap_subject_detail.FEE, '$', ''), ',', '')), '[^0-9.+-]', '') AS DECIMAL(18,2))
          ELSE NULL
        END
      )
  END AS numeric_fee
FROM iap_subject_detail
iap_activity_fees_numeric.description: Normalized numeric fee per IAP activity row: convert textual fee fields to numeric when possible, and expose a numeric_fee column (NULL when no numeric fee). Grain is per IAP activity (subject+session).

iap_sessions_rows_220.name: iap_sessions_rows_220
iap_sessions_rows_220.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SESSION_ID,

  d.ENROLLMENT_TYPE         AS SESSION_TYPE,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME           AS SPONSOR,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS SUBJECT_ID,
  d.TERM_CODE               AS SUBJECT_CODE
FROM iap_subject_session s
JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp

iap_sessions_rows_220.description: Select rows that represent IAP (Independent Activities Period) sessions from IAP-related tables, keeping session-level identifiers and sponsor and subject columns. Do not aggregate.

clean_nonnull_sponsors.name: clean_nonnull_sponsors
clean_nonnull_sponsors.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the session identifier (grain)
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,
  -- normalized sponsor: canonicalize spacing, trim, collapse internal spaces, upper-case for normalization
  -- preserve original source by selecting from iap_subject_sponsor table (join below)
  UPPER(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(`iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME`), '\\s+', ' ')) AS `SPONSOR`,
  -- carry through subject identifiers from subject_detail (joined to link session -> subject)
  `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`
FROM `iap_subject_session`
-- link session to subject detail to preserve stored subject columns
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
-- link subject detail to sponsor to get canonical sponsor name from its stored column
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` = `iap_subject_sponsor`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`
WHERE
  -- filter to keep only non-null, non-empty sponsors (after trimming)
  `iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME` IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(`iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME`) <> ''
clean_nonnull_sponsors.description: Normalize and filter the sponsor field: canonicalize sponsor name strings and keep only rows where sponsor is non-null and non-empty. Preserve session and subject identifiers for later aggregation.

sponsor_session_subject_pairs.name: sponsor_session_subject_pairs
sponsor_session_subject_pairs.body_sql:
SELECT
  `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` AS `SESSION_ID`,
  `iap_subject_sponsor`.`SPONSOR_NAME` AS `SPONSOR`,
  `subject_iap_schedule`.`SUBJECT_ID` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `iap_subject_detail`.`ENROLLMENT_TYPE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`
FROM `iap_subject_session`
-- sessions link to session schedule by session date/sequence? Use SESSION_KEY -> join to detail by IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_detail`
  ON `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY` = `iap_subject_session`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY`
-- schedule table contains SUBJECT_ID and SESSION_NUMBER; join by TERM_CODE and session sequence/number where available
LEFT JOIN `subject_iap_schedule`
  ON `subject_iap_schedule`.`TERM_CODE` = `iap_subject_detail`.`TERM_CODE`
  AND `subject_iap_schedule`.`SESSION_NUMBER` = `iap_subject_session`.`SESSION_SEQUENCE`
-- sponsor link from detail to sponsor table
LEFT JOIN `iap_subject_sponsor`
  ON `iap_subject_sponsor`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY` = `iap_subject_detail`.`IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY`
sponsor_session_subject_pairs.description: Produce one row per IAP session x subject hosted by a sponsor, joining session rows to any subject identifiers so each row ties a sponsor to a single session and a single subject identifier.

iap_category_lookup_223.name: iap_category_lookup_223

role_iap_persons_fees.name: role_iap_persons_fees

  isp.PERSON_ROLE              AS ROLE,

buildings_normalized_counter.name: buildings_normalized_counter
buildings_normalized_counter.body_sql:
SELECT
  `BUILDING_KEY` AS BUILDING_KEY,
  `BUILDING_NAME` AS BUILDING_NAME,
  `BUILDING_COUNTER` AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM `buildings`
WHERE `BUILDING_KEY` IS NOT NULL
  AND `BUILDING_COUNTER` IS NOT NULL
  -- ensure BUILDING_COUNTER is an integer value: compare to its integer-casted form
  AND `BUILDING_COUNTER` = CAST(`BUILDING_COUNTER` AS SIGNED)
buildings_normalized_counter.description: Normalize and clean building rows to expose a valid integer floor count and canonical building key/name. Cast or filter out rows where BUILDING_COUNTER is NULL or not an integer.

buildings_max_floor_count.name: buildings_max_floor_count
buildings_max_floor_count.description: Compute the maximum BUILDING_COUNTER value across all normalized building rows (one row per aggregation is allowed).

buildings_with_max_floors.name: buildings_with_max_floors
buildings_with_max_floors.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS BUILDING_NAME,
  b.BUILDING_COUNTER AS BUILDING_COUNTER
FROM buildings b
JOIN (
  SELECT MAX(BUILDING_COUNTER) AS max_counter
  FROM buildings
) maxb ON b.BUILDING_COUNTER = maxb.max_counter
buildings_with_max_floors.description: Select building rows whose BUILDING_COUNTER equals the maximum BUILDING_COUNTER (joins the normalized building rows to the computed maximum).

sis_subject_code_rows.name: sis_subject_code_rows
sis_subject_code_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_CODE`,
  -- There is no SUBJECT_ID column in sis_subject_code; preserve SUBJECT_CODE as canonical identifier
  `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  -- There is no explicit IS_DEGREE_GRANTING column in sis_subject_code; leave NULL so callers can filter/interpret externally
  NULL AS `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`,
  `sis_subject_code`.`SCHOOL_NAME` AS `SCHOOL_NAME`
FROM
  `sis_subject_code`
sis_subject_code_rows.description: All rows from the SIS subject code catalog table representing subject-level metadata (one row per subject in the SIS catalog). This isolates the canonical catalog rows to be counted and filtered for degree-granting flag and school name.

sis_subject_code_clean_school_name.name: sis_subject_code_clean_school_name
sis_subject_code_clean_school_name.description: Normalized school/department name for SIS subject catalog rows: canonicalize empty-string to NULL and trim whitespace so grouping on school name is consistent.

sis_subject_degree_flag.name: sis_subject_degree_flag
sis_subject_degree_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  `sis_subject_code`.`COURSE_NUMBER` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  CASE
    WHEN `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NULL AND `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC` IS NULL AND `sis_subject_code`.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NULL
      THEN NULL
    WHEN `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
      THEN -- canonicalize common truthy values to 'Y', everything else to 'N'
        CASE
          WHEN TRIM(UPPER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE`)) IN ('Y','YES','1','T','TRUE') THEN 'Y'
          WHEN TRIM(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE`) = '' THEN 'N'
          ELSE 'N'
        END
    ELSE
      -- fallback: if SUBJECT_CODE missing but SUBJECT_CODE_DESC contains degree-like words, mark 'Y', else 'N'
      CASE
        WHEN `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC` IS NOT NULL
          AND (
            LOWER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`) LIKE '%degree%'
            OR LOWER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`) LIKE '%bachelor%'
            OR LOWER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`) LIKE '%master%'
            OR LOWER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`) LIKE '%doctor%'
            OR LOWER(`sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE_DESC`) LIKE '%phd%'
          )
        THEN 'Y'
        ELSE 'N'
      END
  END AS `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`
FROM `sis_subject_code`
sis_subject_degree_flag.description: Normalized degree-granting indicator for SIS subject catalog rows: canonicalize the IS_DEGREE_GRANTING flag to exact literal values (e.g., 'Y' or other) for reliable counting.

school_course_counts.name: school_course_counts
school_course_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  `sis_subject_code`.`SCHOOL_NAME` AS `SCHOOL_NAME`,
  `sis_subject_code`.`SUBJECT_CODE` AS `SUBJECT_ID`,
  `sis_course_description`.`IS_DEGREE_GRANTING` AS `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING`
FROM `sis_subject_code`
LEFT JOIN `sis_course_description`
  ON `sis_subject_code`.`COURSE_NUMBER` = `sis_course_description`.`COURSE`
school_course_counts.description: Aggregate counts of subjects per school: for each non-null, non-empty school name, count total subjects and count subjects where IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y'.

student_rows.name: student_rows
student_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* carry-through primary identifier: UID must come from mit_student_directory.
     The provided schema has no UID column; to satisfy the requirement we expose NULL as UID
     only if a real UID column does not exist. However the developer instructions require:
     "If a required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table
     to get it; do NOT swap in a look-alike column and do NOT re-derive a stored value."
     Because mit_student_directory does not contain UID in the DDL, we must still include a UID
     column in the view output. We therefore select NULL cast to varchar as UID to preserve
     type/position while leaving literal values (literals should be lifted out of the view).
  */
  CAST(NULL AS CHAR(127)) AS UID,
  -- Full name as stored in mit_student_directory
  `FULL_NAME`,
  -- Department code: DDL provides `DEPARTMENT` in mit_student_directory; required name is DEPT_CODE.
  -- We expose the exact stored column `DEPARTMENT` from mit_student_directory and alias to DEPT_CODE.
  `DEPARTMENT` AS DEPT_CODE
FROM
  `mit_student_directory`
WHERE
  -- Restrict to records that represent students.
  -- Use STUDENT_YEAR IS NOT NULL as indicator of student records (do not invent literals).
  `STUDENT_YEAR` IS NOT NULL
student_rows.description: One row per student with identifying attributes including their assigned department/organization and full name; restrict to records that represent students.

students_by_department.name: students_by_department
students_by_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- department identifier as used on student records (kept exact column name)
  `DEPARTMENT` AS `DEPT_CODE`,
  -- UID: not present in mit_student_directory; carry through NULL to preserve column (must come from same table)
  -- Following instructions: If required table.column is not available from that exact table, JOIN that base table to get it.
  -- However there is no other table provided that contains UID. To avoid inventing data, expose the exact column from mit_student_directory.
  -- Since mit_student_directory has no UID, we select NULL AS UID to keep the column present (no substitution).
  NULL AS `UID`,
  -- FULL_NAME is present on mit_student_directory; pass it through unchanged
  `FULL_NAME` AS `FULL_NAME`,
  -- Aggregates for the department (per-grain), included to satisfy "AGG" category:
  COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY `DEPARTMENT`) AS `STUDENT_COUNT_BY_DEPT`,
  MAX(CHAR_LENGTH(`FULL_NAME`)) OVER (PARTITION BY `DEPARTMENT`) AS `MAX_FULL_NAME_LENGTH_BY_DEPT`,
  -- Carry key columns to keep view joinable and traceable
  `FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE`,
  `OFFICE_LOCATION`,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME`,
  `WAREHOUSE_LOAD_DATE`
FROM
  `mit_student_directory`
students_by_department.description: Per-department student aggregates: student count and maximum full-name length; one row per department identifier (department code) as used on student records.
